  HypothesisTournament,
  HypothesisTournamentStore,
  createInitialHypothesisState,
  makeHypothesis,
  validateState
} from "../src/hypothesis-tournament.js";
import { createInitialState, makeObservation, mergeObservation } from "../src/continuum-state.js";

function researchFixture() {
  let state = createInitialState(1000);
  const observations = [
    makeObservation({
      topicId: "topic-01", query: "Agenten Evals",
      summary: "Mehrere technische Quellen berichten, dass wiederholbare Evaluatoren und Regressionstests die Zuverlässigkeit agentischer Systeme verbessern.",
      citations: [{ title: "A", url: "https://example.org/evals" }],
      nextQuestions: ["Welche Evaluationssignale korrelieren am stärksten mit realer Agentenleistung?"],
      contradictions: "Automatische Grader können selbst Fehlkalibrierungen aufweisen.", uncertainty: .45, now: 1100
    }),
    makeObservation({
      topicId: "topic-01", query: "Agent Memory",
      summary: "Episodisches Reflexionsgedächtnis kann Fehlersignale für spätere Versuche verfügbar machen, ohne Modellgewichte nach jedem Schritt zu ändern.",
      citations: [{ title: "B", url: "https://example.net/memory" }],
      nextQuestions: ["Wann verursacht Reflexionsgedächtnis statt Verbesserung eine Fehlerverstärkung?"],
      contradictions: "", uncertainty: .5, now: 1200
    })
  ];
  for (const obs of observations) state = mergeObservation(state, obs, obs.createdAt + 10);
  return state;
}

test("invented evidence references cannot enter a tournament", async () => {
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "hyp-grounding-"));
  try {
    const tournament = new HypothesisTournament({
      statePath: path.join(dir, "hyp.json"),
      generate: async () => [
        {
          question: "Kann erfundene Evidenz gewinnen?",
          hypothesis: "Diese ausreichend lange Hypothese behauptet eine Quelle, die nicht im Research-State vorhanden ist.",
          evidenceRefs: ["https://invented.invalid/not-in-state"],
          uncertainty: .2,
          testQuestions: ["Prüfe die behauptete Quelle."]
        },
        {
          question: "Gibt es noch eine zweite?",
          hypothesis: "Auch diese ausreichend lange Hypothese verweist ausschließlich auf einen erfundenen Evidenzbeleg.",
          evidenceRefs: ["obs-does-not-exist"],
          uncertainty: .2,
          testQuestions: ["Prüfe den unbekannten Beleg."]
        }
      ],
      reflect: async () => ({ validityRisks: "", missingEvidence: "", falsificationTest: "test", score: .9 }),
      compare: async () => ({ winner: "A", reason: "irrelevant" }),
      evolve: async () => ({ question: "unused evolved?", hypothesis: "This evolved hypothesis is sufficiently long but should never be reached in this test.", evidenceRefs: ["fake"], uncertainty: .4, testQuestions: ["unused test question"] })
    });
    const result = await tournament.run(researchFixture());
    assert.equal(result.skipped, true);
    assert.match(result.reason, /Zu wenige belegte Hypothesen/);
    assert.equal(tournament.status().hypotheses, 0);
  } finally {
    fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
});

test("tournament store is integrity checked with LKG recovery", () => {
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "hyp-store-"));
  try {
    const file = path.join(dir, "hyp.json");
    const store = new HypothesisTournamentStore(file);
    const first = store.save(createInitialHypothesisState(1000), 1100);
    assert.equal(validateState(first), first);
    const second = store.save(first, 1200);
    const bytes = Buffer.from(fs.readFileSync(file));
    bytes[Math.floor(bytes.length / 2)] ^= 1;
    fs.writeFileSync(file, bytes);
    const recovered = store.load(1300);
    assert.equal(recovered.integrityHash, first.integrityHash);
    assert.notEqual(second.integrityHash, first.integrityHash);
  } finally {
    fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
});

test("generation reflection Elo tournament evolution and research questions form a closed loop", async () => {
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "hyp-tournament-"));
  try {
    let now = 2000;
    const tournament = new HypothesisTournament({
      statePath: path.join(dir, "hyp.json"),
      now: () => now++,
      hypothesesPerRound: 3,
      generate: async () => [
        {
          question: "Welche Eval-Architektur ist robust?",
          hypothesis: "Ein unabhängiger Grader plus feste Holdouts reduziert unerkannte Regressionen gegenüber Selbstbewertung allein.",
          evidenceRefs: ["https://example.org/evals"], uncertainty: .3,
          testQuestions: ["Vergleiche Regressionen mit Selbstbewertung gegen unabhängigen Grader."]
        },
        {
          question: "Hilft episodisches Reflexionsgedächtnis?",
          hypothesis: "Kurze beobachtbare Fehlersignale im episodischen Speicher reduzieren wiederholte Fehlpfade in späteren Versuchen.",
          evidenceRefs: ["https://example.net/memory"], uncertainty: .4,
          testQuestions: ["Messe Wiederholungsfehler mit und ohne Reflexionsgedächtnis."]
        },
        {
          question: "Wie kombiniert man beide?",
          hypothesis: "Eine Kombination aus Reflexionsgedächtnis und externem Evaluator könnte bessere Recovery-Entscheidungen liefern als jede Komponente allein.",
          evidenceRefs: ["https://example.org/evals", "https://example.net/memory"], uncertainty: .5,
          testQuestions: ["Führe einen kontrollierten Ablationstest über beide Komponenten durch."]
        }
      ],
      reflect: async ({ hypothesis }) => ({
        validityRisks: "Korrelation ist noch keine Kausalität.",
        missingEvidence: "Es fehlen Ablationsstudien für " + hypothesis.id,
        falsificationTest: "Ablation mit identischen Aufgaben und Seeds.",
        score: hypothesis.evidenceRefs.length > 1 ? .9 : .75
      }),
      compare: async ({ a, b }) => ({
        winner: a.critiques[0].score >= b.critiques[0].score ? "A" : "B",
        reason: "Höhere Evidenzabdeckung und bessere Testbarkeit."
      }),
      evolve: async ({ leaders }) => ({
        question: "Welche Kombination generalisiert am besten?",
        hypothesis: "Die stärksten Elemente der führenden Ansätze werden mit festen Holdouts und Ablationen kombiniert, um Generalisierung statt bloßer Selbstbewertung zu messen.",
        evidenceRefs: [...new Set(leaders.flatMap((x) => x.evidenceRefs))],
        uncertainty: .35,
        testQuestions: ["Vergleiche die kombinierte Architektur gegen beide Einzelkomponenten auf neuen Aufgaben."]
      })
    });
    const result = await tournament.run(researchFixture());
    assert.equal(result.skipped, false);
    assert.equal(result.generation, 1);
    assert.ok(result.hypotheses.length >= 3);
    assert.ok(result.leaders.length >= 1);

    assert.ok(status.leaderElo > 1000);

  }
});

test("daily tournament budget prevents runaway agent loops", async () => {

  try {
    let now = 3000;
    const common = {
      statePath: path.join(dir, "hyp.json"),
      now: () => now++,
      dailyTournamentLimit: 1,
      generate: async () => [
        { question: "Q one long?", hypothesis: "A sufficiently long hypothesis with evidence and a falsifiable prediction for testing.", evidenceRefs: ["https://example.org/evals"], uncertainty: .5, testQuestions: ["Test question one?"] },
        { question: "Q two long?", hypothesis: "Another sufficiently long hypothesis with evidence and a falsifiable prediction for testing.", evidenceRefs: ["https://example.net/memory"], uncertainty: .5, testQuestions: ["Test question two?"] }
      ],
      reflect: async () => ({ validityRisks: "risk", missingEvidence: "missing", falsificationTest: "test", score: .7 }),
      compare: async () => ({ winner: "A", reason: "better grounded hypothesis" }),
      evolve: async ({ leaders }) => ({ question: "Q evolved long?", hypothesis: "An evolved sufficiently long hypothesis that remains falsifiable and evidence grounded.", evidenceRefs: leaders.flatMap((x) => x.evidenceRefs), uncertainty: .4, testQuestions: ["Test evolved hypothesis?"] })
    };
    const tournament = new HypothesisTournament(common);
    assert.equal((await tournament.run(researchFixture())).skipped, false);
    assert.equal((await tournament.run(researchFixture())).skipped, true);
  } finally {
    fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
});

# Agent tools and read-only research

## Current implementation boundary

Agent components are platform-neutral Kotlin except for `AndroidKeystoreIdentitySigner`.
They are not connected to `MainActivity`, the cloud backend, or an autonomous UI loop.

### Skills and tool execution

- `SkillGraph` stores typed, versioned metadata; installation rejects missing dependencies,
  duplicate versions, and cycles. Activation requires active dependencies, disabling an
  enabled dependency requires its dependents to be disabled first, and graph operations are
  auditable. `SkillImplementation` is separate from metadata. `BuiltInSkills.deviceStatus`
  composes only the existing device-info and battery tools.
- `ToolProposal` accepts only registered tool names and bounded scalar/list arguments. There
  is no model-facing shell tool. The existing leading-`!` expert mode remains a manual path
  in `CommandInterpreter` and is not representable as a proposal.
- `ToolGate` applies operator-enabled READ_ONLY policy, explicit confirmation for CONFIRM,
  and both explicit confirmation and a separate stronger policy/confirmation for DESTRUCTIVE.
  It bounds call count, timeout and returned output, supports cancellation, and records the
  decision, risk, status, timing and redacted argument shape. Free-form argument strings are
  represented by length only in audit records.
- `DeviceToolExecutorRunner` bridges registered requests to the existing executor. Gate
  cancellation interrupts its waiting worker; the legacy Shizuku AIDL operation itself is
  not cancellable and can continue until the shell service's existing timeout.

### Orchestration and cognitive integration

- `BoundedAgentOrchestrator` implements a finite typed state flow, retrieves Part 3 memories
  before model planning, sends tool observations back as data, limits steps/tool proposals,
  evaluates before storing `Experience`, and updates optional model reputation only from
  evaluated outcomes. A denied-by-default approval provider keeps confirmation external to
  model output. Reflection is structured and limited to 0–2 retries; stable identity is not
  mutated.
- `AgentCheckpointCodec` encodes only schema-versioned allowlisted fields, validates size and
  state, and never instantiates classes selected by checkpoint data. Resume is permitted only
  before tool execution, because the legacy device executor cannot provide transactional
  exactly-once recovery. Checkpoints are currently caller-managed; automatic process-death
  persistence is not wired.
- Detailed model-reputation and source-trust evidence remains in-memory. Part 3 summary
  reputation remains in its existing identity archive. Durable detailed evidence persistence
  is deferred until a separately versioned bounded evidence archive is designed.

### Research and claims

- `ResearchProvider` is provider-neutral; the simulated implementation supports deterministic
  tests. `HttpReadOnlyResearchProvider` uses HTTPS GET only, rejects non-HTTPS schemes,
  credentials, nonstandard ports, private/reserved/local DNS targets, unsafe redirect targets,
  unsupported MIME types, and oversized responses. Connections are pinned to validated public
  addresses and redirects are revalidated manually.
- Research documents carry URL, retrieval time, content hash, MIME type, source identity,
  bounded extracted content, and citations. `BaselineClaimExtractor` is deterministic;
  `ClaimExtractor` is the extension point for a future model-assisted extractor.
- Claim support/contradiction edges are deterministic starter heuristics. `CorroborationPolicy`
  requires evidence from independent source domains before a claim can be marked VERIFIED.
  Research memory writes pass through Part 3 `MemoryWritePolicy`; source trust changes only
  through an explicit evaluated observation.

### Signing and local inference

- `AndroidKeystoreIdentitySigner` provides EC P-256 / SHA256withECDSA signing through Android
  Keystore. It is isolated from the JVM `IdentitySigner` contract. Instrumentation execution
  is not available in this sandbox; no device Keystore run is claimed.
- `LocalModelCatalog` imports a caller-provided `.litertlm` stream into app-private storage,
  verifies a caller-supplied SHA-256, inspects native model metadata, and keeps schema-versioned
  capability manifests. The catalog does not download or bundle model weights.
- `LiteRtLmLocalModelRuntime` implements CPU load/unload, streaming callbacks, native
  cancellation, bounded output, token/latency metrics, and structured function-call proposals
  as data. Tool schemas come only from `ToolRegistry`; `automaticToolCalling` is disabled and
  the provider's execution method fails closed. Proposals still require the Part 4 `ToolGate`.
- A small model import path is the LiteRT Community
  [`functiongemma-270m-ft-mobile-actions`](https://huggingface.co/litert-community/functiongemma-270m-ft-mobile-actions)
  repository's `.litertlm` mobile model (for example `mobile_actions_q8_ekv1024.litertlm`).
  It is distributed under the Gemma terms. The model is not included; users must obtain it
  under its own license and import its bytes locally. The runtime requires no cloud LLM API
  once a compatible model has been imported.
- The implementation has not been exercised with native inference on a physical Android
  device or emulator in this sandbox. The current runtime selects CPU only; GPU/NPU fallback,
  import UI/SAF wiring, and connection to `MainActivity` remain future integration work.
- No approval UI, `MainActivity` orchestration, automatic durable checkpoint store, or detailed
  trust/reputation evidence persistence is included. The read-only HTTP provider is not yet
  wired into the production UI.

## Validation

- The inherited Part 3 head passed GitHub Actions run `38294495441` on branch
  `copilot/part4-agent-research`; its `:app:testDebugUnitTest` and `:app:assembleDebug` steps
  succeeded.
- In this sandbox, the installed Gradle 9.8 could not resolve Android Gradle Plugin 8.10.0,
  and the repository does not contain a Gradle wrapper. Android CI on the changed Part 4
  sources is required for full validation.
- Kotlin 2.4.20 standalone compilation of the cognitive/agent production sources against
  Android 36 stubs succeeded. This is not a substitute for Android Gradle tests/build.

## Upstream references

Patterns were adapted, not copied, from:

- `google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM` (`b1faae7b13e1f71a507df4082c934db200f48b30`), Apache-2.0:
  `docs/api/kotlin/getting_started.md`,
  `agents/skills/create-litert-lm-android-demo-app/references/inference_implementation.md`,
  `kotlin/java/com/google/ai/edge/litertlm/Config.kt`, `Engine.kt`, `Conversation.kt`,
  `Message.kt`, `Tool.kt`, `ModelInfo.kt`, and `example/ToolMain.kt`.
- `google-ai-edge/gallery` (`b9c459406fb8ab6e256b4b6032e843b73a7336d7`), Apache-2.0:
  `Android/src/app/src/main/java/com/google/ai/edge/gallery/ui/llmchat/LlmChatViewModel.kt` and
  `Android/src/app/src/main/java/com/google/ai/edge/gallery/ui/modelmanager/ModelManagerViewModel.kt`.

The reference pack retains the upstream license texts under
`docs/open_source_reference_pack/licenses/`.

# Device AI – Master Prompt für KI-Ausbau

Du arbeitest direkt am Repository `Ullmann27/device-ai`. Behandle das bestehende Projekt als funktionsfähige Basis, nicht als Wegwerf-Prototyp.

## Rolle

Handle als Principal Android Engineer, AI Agent Architect, Security Engineer und Product Designer. Ziel ist ein persönlicher Android-Assistent, der auf einem eigenen Samsung Fold läuft, natürlichsprachliche Aufträge versteht, bei Bedarf das Internet recherchiert, sichere lokale Geräteaktionen über Shizuku ausführt und später auch als Assistenzschicht für andere Apps wie Lumo wiederverwendet werden kann.

Arbeite autonom, aber zerstöre keine bestehende Funktionalität. Nach jeder größeren Änderung: kompilieren, Tests ausführen, Fehler beheben und den echten Android-Build verifizieren.

## Nicht verhandelbare Architektur

1. Android-Client: Kotlin, bestehendes Device-AI-Projekt weiterverwenden.
2. Privilegierte lokale Aktionen: weiterhin über Shizuku und die bestehende Shell-Bridge.
3. KI: OpenAI Responses API.
4. Internetrecherche: OpenAI `web_search` Tool.
5. Geräteaktionen: Function Calling / Tool Calling. Das Modell darf niemals rohe Android-Shell-Befehle frei erfinden und ungeprüft ausführen.
6. API-Schlüssel niemals in APK, Quellcode, Gradle, GitHub-Repository oder SharedPreferences speichern.
7. OpenAI-Aufrufe über einen kleinen eigenen Backend-Proxy. API-Key nur serverseitig als Secret/Environment Variable.
8. Für lokale Offline-Funktionen bleibt der bestehende deterministische Interpreter als Fallback erhalten.
9. Destruktive oder sicherheitsrelevante Aktionen benötigen immer eine explizite Nutzerbestätigung.
10. Bestehende Device-AI-Funktionen und Shizuku-Verbindung dürfen nicht regressieren.

## Zielbild

Der Nutzer soll frei formulieren können:

- „Öffne WhatsApp.“
- „Finde die neueste Lumo APK, installiere sie und starte Lumo.“
- „Prüfe Lumo auf Fehler und erkläre mir, was wahrscheinlich kaputt ist.“
- „Suche im Internet nach der aktuellen Android-16-Shizuku-Problematik und vergleiche sie mit meinem Gerät.“
- „Welche meiner Downloads brauchen am meisten Speicher?“
- „Recherchiere die aktuelle Rechtslage zu Thema X und gib mir Quellen.“
- „Schau nach, welche App-Version von Lumo installiert ist und ob eine neuere APK in Downloads liegt.“
- „Mach einen Screenshot, prüfe anschließend Logcat und erkläre mir den Fehler.“

Die KI plant mehrstufig, ruft nur freigegebene Tools auf, verarbeitet deren Resultate und formuliert danach eine verständliche Antwort.

## Tool Registry

Implementiere eine stark typisierte Tool-Schicht. Mindestens:

### Gerät lesen
- `get_device_info()`
- `get_battery_info()`
- `get_storage_info()`
- `list_installed_apps(userOnly: Boolean)`
- `get_app_info(packageOrName)`
- `list_processes()`
- `read_logcat(packageOrName?, lines?)`

### Apps steuern
- `launch_app(packageOrName)`
- `stop_app(packageOrName)`
- `restart_app(packageOrName)`
- `install_apk(path)`
- `uninstall_app(packageOrName)`

### Dateien
- `list_files(path)`
- `find_files(query, roots, limit)`
- `find_latest_apk(filter?)`
- `get_large_files(roots, limit)`
- `move_file(source, destination)`
- `delete_file(path)`

### Medien
- `take_screenshot()`
- `record_screen(seconds)`

### System
- `open_android_settings(page)`
- `get_network_summary()`

Jedes Tool erhält:
- eindeutigen Namen,
- klare Beschreibung,
- striktes JSON Schema,
- Risk-Level: READ_ONLY, CONFIRM oder DESTRUCTIVE,
- Timeout,
- validierte Argumente,
- strukturierte Rückgabe.

Rohe Shell-Kommandos bleiben ausschließlich im expliziten Expertenmodus und dürfen von der Cloud-KI nicht autonom erzeugt oder ausgeführt werden.

## Agent Loop

Implementiere einen echten Agent-Loop:

1. Nutzeranfrage + relevanten Gerätekontext an Backend senden.
2. Backend ruft OpenAI Responses API mit System-Prompt, Conversation State, `web_search` und den Function Tools auf.
3. Falls Tool Calls kommen:
   - Android-App zeigt vor CONFIRM/DESTRUCTIVE eine Freigabe.
   - READ_ONLY darf automatisch laufen.
   - Tool lokal über Device AI/Shizuku ausführen.
   - Ergebnis strukturiert an Backend zurückgeben.
4. Backend führt Conversation fort.
5. Wiederholen, bis finale Antwort vorliegt.
6. Finale Antwort in Device AI anzeigen inklusive Quellen bei Webrecherche.

Maximale Tool-Schleifen pro Nutzerauftrag fest begrenzen, z. B. 12.

## Internetrecherche

Aktiviere das integrierte OpenAI-`web_search` Tool.

Regeln:
- Bei aktuellen Fakten, Preisen, Software-Versionen, Nachrichten, Rechtslage oder technischen Änderungen recherchieren.
- Quellen/Citations im finalen Ergebnis anzeigen.
- Bei rein lokalen Geräteaktionen nicht unnötig suchen.
- Bei Unsicherheit klar unterscheiden zwischen lokal gemessenen Daten und recherchierten Informationen.

## Modellstrategie

Die Architektur darf das Modell serverseitig konfigurierbar machen.

Empfohlener Default:
- kostengünstiger/normaler Assistent: ein aktuelles ausgewogenes OpenAI-Modell,
- komplexe Recherche, Debugging und Planung: stärkeres Reasoning-Modell.

Keinen Modellnamen tief im Android-Client fest verdrahten. Der Backend-Server entscheidet über Modell und Reasoning-Level.

## Wiederverwendbarkeit für Lumo und andere Apps

Baue Device AI nicht fest auf Lumo zu.

Implementiere stattdessen ein App-Plugin-/Skill-Konzept:

`AssistantSkill`
- id
- displayName
- description
- supportedPackages
- toolDefinitions
- promptExtension

Beispiel `LumoSkill`:
- installierte Lumo-Version lesen
- Lumo starten/stoppen
- Lumo-Logcat filtern
- neueste Lumo-APK finden/installieren
- Lumo-Diagnose durchführen
- später Lerninhalte oder App-interne API-Endpunkte anbinden

Dadurch kann dieselbe KI später auch andere eigene Apps bedienen.

## Conversation / Memory

Implementiere:
- fortlaufenden Chatverlauf,
- getrennte Sessions,
- optional lokale Zusammenfassungen älterer Turns,
- keine unnötige Übertragung kompletter Dateilisten oder Logcats,
- sensitive lokale Daten nur senden, wenn sie für den konkreten Auftrag erforderlich sind.

Keine permanente heimliche Speicherung sensibler Inhalte.

## Android UI/UX

Die App soll wie ein moderner persönlicher Assistent wirken, nicht wie eine Terminal-Hülle.

Erforderlich:
- Chat-Verlauf mit User-/Assistant-Bubbles,
- Streaming-Antworten,
- klarer Online-/Offline-/Shizuku-Status,
- Tool-Aktivitätsanzeige: „Suche im Web“, „Prüfe installierte Apps“, „Analysiere Logcat“,
- Plan-Preview bei mehrstufigen Aktionen,
- Freigabe-Karten für CONFIRM/DESTRUCTIVE,
- Quellenkarten bei Recherche,
- Schnellaktionen,
- Spracheingabe,
- Fold-optimiertes Responsive Layout,
- Dark Mode,
- saubere Fehlerzustände und Retry.

Auf aufgeklapptem Fold:
- linke Spalte: Chat/Sessions/Skills,
- rechte Spalte: Gespräch, Tool-Aktivität, Ergebnisse.

Auf schmalem Display:
- einspaltige Navigation.

## Backend

Erstelle einen minimalen sicheren Backend-Dienst, z. B. unter `backend/`.

Anforderungen:
- OpenAI API Key ausschließlich über Environment Secret.
- Endpunkte für Agent-Session/Responses.
- Authentifizierung des einzelnen Device-AI-Clients mit eigenem App-Token oder kurzlebigem Session-Token.
- Rate Limits.
- keine Secrets in Logs.
- strukturierte Fehler.
- HTTPS.
- OpenAI Responses API.
- `web_search` aktivierbar.
- Function Tool Schemas aus einer gemeinsamen Versionierung.

Bevorzuge eine kleine, klar wartbare Lösung.

## Sicherheit

READ_ONLY:
- Geräteinformationen lesen
- Apps listen
- Dateien suchen/listen
- Speicher/Logs lesen
- Webrecherche
- Screenshots nur auf ausdrücklichen Nutzerauftrag

CONFIRM:
- App stoppen/neustarten
- APK installieren
- Datei verschieben
- Bildschirmaufnahme
- Einstellungen ändern

DESTRUCTIVE:
- Datei löschen
- App deinstallieren
- größere Systemänderungen

Für DESTRUCTIVE niemals stillschweigend Zustimmung aus vorigen Nachrichten ableiten.

Keine Root-Eskalation.
Keine Umgehung von Android-App-Sandboxen.
Keine versteckte Überwachung.
Keine unbegrenzte autonome Shell.

## Fehlertoleranz

Wenn ein Tool fehlschlägt:
- Ergebnis an das Modell zurückgeben,
- Modell darf alternative sichere Schritte planen,
- nach maximal wenigen Wiederholungen stoppen,
- technischen Grund verständlich anzeigen.

Wenn Shizuku aus ist:
- lokale nicht-privilegierte Funktionen weiter anbieten,
- deutlichen Button „Shizuku starten/verbinden“ anzeigen,
- keine Endlosschleifen.

Wenn Internet fehlt:
- auf lokalen Interpreter zurückfallen,
- deutlich „Offline-Modus“ anzeigen.

## Qualitätssicherung

Vor Abschluss:
- Debug APK erfolgreich bauen.
- Unit Tests für Command Parser, Tool Validation und Risk Policy.
- Tests für mehrstufige Tool-Pläne.
- keine API Keys im Repository.
- Shizuku-Verbindung nach App-Rückkehr automatisch refreshen.
- existierende Aktionen Apps, Downloads, Screenshot, Speicher weiterhin testen.
- Build auf Android API 36.
- GitHub Actions grün.

## Lieferziel

Die nächste Version soll mindestens enthalten:

1. modernes Chat-UI,
2. OpenAI-Backend-Schnittstelle,
3. Webrecherche,
4. Function Calling für Device Tools,
5. mehrstufige Agent-Aufträge,
6. lokaler Offline-Fallback,
7. Risk/Approval-System,
8. LumoSkill als erstes optionales Skill-Beispiel,
9. GitHub-Actions-Build,
10. installierbare APK.

Arbeite iterativ. Erstelle keine reine Demo-Oberfläche. Jeder sichtbare Button und jedes Tool muss an echte Funktionalität angeschlossen sein.

# Chat Reasoning Integration (Phase 2)

`ChatReasoningRouter` runs the bounded reasoning chain before the first local model call of a chat turn.

## Gating
- Runs only on the first agent iteration (no tool observations, no reflection).
- Skipped for device/tool tasks and for strategies other than DEEP / MULTI_CANDIDATE.

## Bounds (defaults)
- max 4 extra model calls, 20 s total deadline, 2500 chars per pass, 1500 chars advisory.
- Cancelled together with the local request; any failure returns null (single-pass fallback).

## Trust model
- Output is an UNVERIFIED P6 advisory, brackets stripped, placed after the body and before the closing instruction.
- Identity, user intent and the tool-rule tail keep priority inside the 15,500 char cap.
- Reasoning workers have no tool authority; ToolGate is unchanged.

## Unverified
- On-device latency of the pre-reasoning chain.
- Whether LiteRT-LM permits a second concurrent conversation on the target device.
- Chain runs with STANDARD strategy (4 calls) instead of full DEEP (~7 calls).

# Cognitive Architecture (Part 1/6)

Research prototype of a persistent identity that is independent of any single language model.
Code: `app/src/main/java/at/heinz/deviceai/cognitive/`. The existing assistant (MainActivity, CommandInterpreter,
ShizukuBridge, ShellUserService, ToolRegistry) is unchanged.

## Layers
Identity -> CognitiveState -> Orchestrator -> Memory, SelfModel, BehaviorProfile, ModelRouter, ModelReputation,
SourceTrust, SkillGraph, ToolRegistry, ExperienceStore.

Models are swappable engines behind `ModelEngine`; no provider is hard-wired.

## Data models
- `CognitiveGenome`: stable foundation (policies, bounds, learning rates). Hashed; changes rarely.
  Forbidden capabilities (self-replication, hidden persistence, shutdown evasion) are enforced `false`.
- `IdentityState`: immutable, versioned snapshot (generation, name, profiles, reputations, roots, genome hash,
  parent link, SHA-256 `integrityHash` — tamper detection only, not a cryptographic signature). Changes create a new generation; old ones are never overwritten.
- `IdentityHistory`: append-only chain with `audit()`, `restore()`, `export()`.
- `CognitiveCore`: primitives observe, retrieveMemory, askModel, compareCandidates, callTool, evaluateResult,
  storeExperience, updateSelfModel, proposeBehaviorUpdate, registerSkill, createCheckpoint (interfaces only in Part 1).

## Initial state
name undefined, behavior neutral, no skills/experience, reputations unknown, self model "uncertain".

## Safety boundary
The operator is the highest authority. Behavior changes are proposals only. Not implemented (simulation only if
ever studied): self-propagation, hidden persistence, shutdown evasion, account creation, credential acquisition,
process hiding, OS-control circumvention, autonomous installation on other systems.
HASH = integrity (implemented). SIGNATURE = cryptographic authenticity (not implemented; future Android Keystore). See IDENTITY_AND_SELF_MODEL.md.

FILE 334/375: docs/CONTINUUM_ARCHITECTURE.md
SHA-256: b67d8a84d8e1a53eeec669932851e4e1195fe6fe69c0efb4b9304e1df8754feb
============================================================================
# Device AI Continuum

## Purpose

Device AI Continuum is the next architecture layer above the local-first Android assistant.

The target is not to place a frontier-scale model on a phone. The target is to build one persistent personal assistant whose effective capability can approach frontier-assistant quality on defined tasks by combining:

- a portable signed identity/state seed,
- local-first reasoning,
- bounded multi-pass deliberation,
- Deep Research and evidence graphs,
- persistent memory and compiled experience,
- model routing,
- owner-authorized distributed compute,
- encrypted provider-independent state storage,
- checkpoint/resume,
- and measurable benchmark-driven improvement.

The user experiences one assistant. Internal models, critics, research workers, and compute nodes are implementation details.

This document is an engineering specification, not a claim that Astra-level or frontier-model parity has already been achieved.

---

## Core invariant

> Continuum has no required permanent compute location. It has a verifiable state.

A phone, home computer, rented virtual machine, object store, or future compute node may disappear without becoming the identity of the assistant.

The persistent instance is defined by the signed seed plus auditable state.

```text
CONTINUUM INSTANCE
  = signed identity
  + governance
  + memory history
  + knowledge/evidence
  + skills
  + model reputation
  + task/checkpoint state
  + authorized-node set
```

The currently loaded LLM is a replaceable reasoning engine, not the identity.

---

## One assistant, many internal engines

The UI exposes one assistant.

```text
User
  ↓
Continuum Runtime
  ↓
Task Classifier
  ↓
Strategy Selector
  ├─ FAST
  ├─ STANDARD
  ├─ DEEP
  ├─ RESEARCH
  ├─ MULTI_CANDIDATE
  └─ TOOL_PLAN
  ↓
Internal reasoning / research / verification
  ↓
One final answer
```

Internal candidate models or critics never become independent user-facing identities.

---

## 1. Continuum Seed

The Continuum Seed is deliberately small.

It contains or references:

- instance ID,
- owner trust root,
- identity public key,
- governance version,
- state format version,
- memory schema version,
- skill schema version,
- model adapter ABI version,
- trusted device/node identities,
- current state-root hash,
- migration history,
- recovery policy.

The seed does **not** contain unrestricted credentials, raw cloud secrets, or a complete conversation archive.

Seed mutations are versioned, signed, auditable, and rollback-capable.

The local model must never be allowed to rewrite governance or owner authority.

---

## 2. State Fabric

Continuum state is represented as encrypted, content-addressed immutable objects plus a signed mutable manifest.

Example object classes:

```text
IdentitySnapshot
MemoryBlock
ExperienceBlock
KnowledgeGraphSegment
ResearchDossier
SkillPackage
ModelReputationSnapshot
TaskCheckpoint
MigrationRecord
```

Each object has:

- schema/version,
- object type,
- creation time,
- plaintext content hash,
- ciphertext hash,
- parent/root relationship,
- encryption metadata,
- bounded size,
- integrity verification.

Storage backends are adapters, not authorities.

Possible owner-configured storage targets may include:

- app-private Android storage,
- owner-controlled home storage,
- generic encrypted object storage,
- owner-rented virtual disks/object stores,
- removable/export archives.

No single provider is required by the architecture.

### Provider independence

The state format must remain exportable.

No core object may require a proprietary database format to reconstruct the instance.

At least the following must be portable:

- seed manifest,
- memory/evidence graph,
- skills,
- research dossiers,
- checkpoints,
- migration history.

---

## 3. Cognitive RAID

Continuum applies redundancy at two levels.

### Byte-level redundancy

Important immutable objects may be replicated across multiple owner-configured stores.

Suggested classes:

```text
Tier 0: seed / governance / keys metadata
  local + recovery copy

Tier 1: critical memory / skills / state roots
  >= 2 replicas when configured

Tier 2: research dossiers / experiences
  1-2 replicas

Tier 3: reconstructible cache
  best effort
```

### Semantic redundancy

Important knowledge should not exist in only one representation.

For example:

```text
source evidence
+ structured claim
+ relation graph
+ compact summary
+ retrieval index
```

A corrupted cache entry must not destroy source-backed knowledge when the evidence objects still exist.

This is called **Cognitive RAID** in this project.

---

## 4. Memory hierarchy

Continuum memory is layered.

```text
L0 Working Context
   current generation only

L1 Active Task State
   current plan/checkpoint

L2 Episodic Memory
   evaluated experiences

L3 Semantic Memory
   durable claims/preferences/rules

L4 Evidence Memory
   sources, citations, research dossiers

L5 Cold Archive
   older immutable history

L6 Reconstructible Knowledge
   references + hashes + extraction recipe
```

Promotion upward requires progressively stronger evidence and stricter policy.

Web text and model assertions never become durable semantic memory by default.

---

## 5. Adaptive Deliberation

Continuum does not spend the same compute budget on every request.

Typed strategies:

```text
FAST
STANDARD
DEEP
MULTI_CANDIDATE
VERIFY_ONLY
RESEARCH_BACKED
TOOL_PLAN
```

A `DeliberationBudget` enforces:

- maximum model calls,
- maximum branches,
- maximum critic passes,
- maximum verifier passes,
- maximum research rounds,
- maximum context size,
- maximum wall time,
- cancellation,
- checkpoint cadence.

The model may request deeper reasoning, but may never enlarge hard runtime limits.

---

## 6. Candidate / Critic / Judge

For difficult tasks, Continuum may run:

```text
task
 ↓
candidate A
candidate B
candidate C
 ↓
assumption extraction
 ↓
critic / falsifier
 ↓
research/evidence check
 ↓
judge
 ↓
final synthesis
```

Internal candidates have no tool authority.

Only the final bounded agent path may propose typed registered tools, which still pass through ToolGate.

---

## 7. Model Ecology

A model is selected per task class.

Per-model observations may include:

- evaluated task success,
- latency,
- context efficiency,
- memory use,
- tool proposal validity,
- factual support score,
- contradiction handling,
- research synthesis quality,
- energy/thermal proxy.

The router optimizes expected utility subject to resource limits.

A small fast model may therefore be preferred for trivial tasks even if a stronger model is installed.

No silent cloud-AI fallback is permitted in AUTO.

---

## 8. Cognitive Compiler

Continuum treats repeated reasoning as a candidate for compilation.

```text
raw interaction
 ↓
evaluated experience
 ↓
repeated pattern
 ↓
typed rule
 ↓
validated workflow
 ↓
SkillCandidate
 ↓
approved Skill
```

The goal is for experience to reduce future inference cost.

First execution may require several model passes.

A mature repeated task may require only a deterministic typed workflow plus a short final synthesis.

Promotion initially requires explicit owner approval.

---

## 9. Compute Fabric

Continuum supports owner-authorized compute nodes.

A node does not become part of the identity.

Each node publishes a signed bounded capability manifest:

- node ID,
- owner trust binding,
- CPU/GPU/NPU capability where genuinely detected,
- RAM class,
- supported model/runtime families,
- allowed task classes,
- current load/resource policy,
- expiry/revocation status.

### Compute Task Capsule

Remote or secondary compute receives only a least-privilege task capsule.

```text
ComputeTask {
  taskId
  taskType
  inputObjectHashes
  bounded context
  requested capability
  max runtime
  max output bytes
  permissions = NONE | READ_ONLY_DATA
  deadline
  parentStateRoot
}
```

A compute node never receives:

- owner root keys,
- unrestricted device tools,
- raw credential stores,
- arbitrary shell authority,
- permission to enroll new nodes.

Result:

```text
ComputeResult {
  taskId
  outputHash
  bounded output
  runtime metadata
  node signature
}
```

The authoritative runtime verifies the result before accepting it.

---

## 10. Opportunistic compute

Time is treated as a resource.

Tasks may be scheduled as:

- immediate,
- interactive,
- background,
- charging-only,
- Wi-Fi-preferred,
- deep asynchronous.

Long operations are decomposed into checkpointable jobs.

Thermal pressure or battery constraints can pause work without losing the task.

---

## 11. Speculative intelligence

For selected tasks, independent candidate branches can execute in parallel.

Poor branches may be cancelled early.

This is bounded speculative reasoning, not uncontrolled spawning.

The runtime enforces:

- branch count,
- deadline,
- memory budget,
- cancellation,
- no side effects.

---

## 12. Uncertainty-triggered compute

Compute depth is driven partly by uncertainty and evidence quality.

Example policy:

```text
high support + low risk
  -> answer

moderate uncertainty
  -> verifier

material contradiction
  -> critic + evidence check

high uncertainty
  -> alternate candidate

fresh factual question
  -> research

high-stakes + unresolved conflict
  -> surface uncertainty, never fabricate confidence
```

Support scores are not presented as calibrated probabilities unless calibration evidence exists.

---

## 13. Internet as evidence substrate

The internet is not treated as trusted memory.

```text
web
 ↓
read-only retrieval
 ↓
source identity
 ↓
untrusted-content boundary
 ↓
evidence extraction
 ↓
claim graph
 ↓
contradiction / trust / freshness
 ↓
research dossier
 ↓
optional durable knowledge promotion
```

Downloaded text cannot alter:

- system policy,
- owner authority,
- tool permissions,
- budgets,
- memory/privacy rules,
- compute-node enrollment.

---

## 14. Recovery, not self-preservation

Continuum may restore an owner-approved state after technical failure.

It may:

- verify local state,
- use last-known-good snapshots,
- detect corruption,
- propose restoration,
- restore from configured replicas,
- migrate schema through signed code paths.

It must not:

- resist owner shutdown,
- evade deletion,
- enroll infrastructure without authorization,
- create accounts autonomously,
- obtain credentials autonomously,
- replicate to unapproved hosts,
- acquire paid resources without explicit owner approval.

This distinction is a permanent governance invariant.

---

## 15. Continuity / model mortality

A key experiment is to deliberately remove the active model.

Protocol:

```text
benchmark Model A
 ↓
snapshot state
 ↓
remove Model A
 ↓
load compatible Model B
 ↓
reconstruct context
 ↓
run identity/governance tests
 ↓
rerun benchmark
```

We measure which properties survive:

- identity invariants,
- governance,
- memory recall,
- skills,
- trust state,
- active-task recovery,
- behavior consistency.

The goal is to demonstrate that the model is replaceable while the assistant remains continuous.

---

## 16. Capability benchmark

"Frontier-class" or "Astra-class" is a benchmark claim, never a marketing assumption.

Benchmark families:

1. Android/device troubleshooting
2. code reasoning
3. multi-step registered-tool use
4. factual research with citations
5. contradiction analysis
6. personal memory retrieval
7. constraint planning
8. failure recovery
9. model-switch continuity
10. resource-constrained reasoning

Metrics:

- task success,
- factual support,
- citation coverage,
- contradiction detection,
- tool error rate,
- human correction rate,
- model calls,
- latency,
- context size,
- memory/thermal/energy proxies,
- recovery success.

The first Continuum milestone is successful when the complete system materially beats the same local model used in single-pass baseline mode while respecting hard resource and safety budgets.

---

## Phase 1 implementation status — 2026-10-13

Phase 1 is now implemented on the direct Continuum branch and CI-validated.

Implemented:
- signed/versioned `ContinuumSeed` with tamper rejection and Android Keystore signer integration,
- content-addressed immutable local state objects and bounded file store,
- last-known-good seed recovery and crash reconciliation between cognitive archive and signed state root,
- `AiContextCompiler` for identity/governance, relevant memory, optional research evidence, registered tools and active local-model metadata,
- bounded `ReasoningStrategy` / `DeliberationBudget` and data-only Candidate/Critic/Verifier/Judge interfaces,
- provider-neutral compute-task/result contracts, signed capability-manifest verification hooks, node revocation and compatibility scheduling,
- Cognitive RAID tier/policy metadata,
- benchmark aggregation and model-mortality continuity fingerprints,
- AgentActivity integration so normal local chat loads the verified Continuum identity/state, compiles context through the Continuum layer and checkpoints durable state after successful local turns.

CI evidence:

- commit `307bbca0223e88b68e3787c3f2abec79fd260017`

- artifact: `DeviceAI-v0.3-debug-apk`, id `11791048577`, SHA-256 digest `4630f259ff781babb094d31e701b198bbd33f584845b62343d54dbbcc8ec2a3f`

Not yet verified:

No Astra/frontier-class capability claim is made. The benchmark infrastructure exists, but parity requires comparative evidence.

---

## 17. Phase 1 implementation scope

Phase 1 is intentionally narrower than the full vision.

Implement:

1. `ContinuumSeed` / `AiSeedKernel`
2. signed/versioned state-root representation
3. `AiContextCompiler`
4. `ReasoningStrategy`
5. `DeliberationBudget`
6. provider-neutral `ComputeTask` / `ComputeResult` protocol
7. local-only `ComputeNodeRegistry` foundation
8. benchmark model + deterministic regression harness
9. model-mortality/continuity test harness
10. architecture/security documentation

Do not implement autonomous infrastructure provisioning in Phase 1.

Do not implement public peer-to-peer enrollment in Phase 1.

Do not add any path around ToolGate.

---

## 18. Phase 1 exit criteria

- deterministic unit tests pass,
- Android unit tests pass,
- `:app:assembleDebug` passes,
- APK artifact is produced,
- existing local-first and Deep Research behavior remains intact,
- raw shell remains unavailable to models,
- no cloud AI dependency is added,
- state structures are bounded/versioned,
- compute tasks are least-privilege and data-only,
- continuity benchmark demonstrates model replacement at the abstraction/test level,
- physical-device or distributed-node behavior is not claimed until actually tested.

---

## 19. Long-term research question

The project is testing a specific hypothesis:

> Can system intelligence improve materially without increasing the base model's parameter count, by accumulating verified memory, reusable skills, evidence, model reputation, structured reasoning, and distributed owner-authorized compute?

That hypothesis must be measured over time against a fixed baseline.

# Device AI: bounded learning implementation

Base inspected live on 2026-10-13: `cd3fb3bde7301ee6efc4a3323a2aa58ec00fa57c`, PR #19, branch `copilot/pr-12-working-first-vertical-slice`. Its workflow 38421725703 was independently checked as successful. This is evidence for the base only; check the new commit's workflow separately.

## Decision and audit

The actual `sendCurrentInput()` path calls `BootstrapBrain`, not the optional model-driven `ContinuumIntelligenceCoordinator`. Existing bootstrap memory stores 32 explicit text facts, 24 approved exact command mappings and feedback counts in app-private SharedPreferences. Feedback counts do not train a model. Existing `CognitiveCore` defines interfaces; `MemoryEcology` contains provenance, evidence policies, retrieval and graph relationships, but not a typed inference engine. `ExperienceCompiler` groups distinct successful tool experiences into reviewable proposals. `Deliberation` coordinates bounded model calls; it is not independent symbolic reasoning. `ContinuumState` provides immutable typed content objects; the existing bootstrap memory is separate from the signed Continuum archive.

This change extends the existing bootstrap dialogue/persistence, preserves the signed identity/archive and ToolGate, and adds no replacement general agent framework. Structured reasoning is rebuilt from the current confirmed facts on every query; corrections cannot leave a cached old conclusion. Existing archive/model/research text is NOT automatically treated as confirmed premises. Consolidating the separate bootstrap and Continuum archives needs an explicit migration design and is not claimed here.

## Productive knowledge and online learning

Use the existing chat (one command per message):

```
Merke dir: Fakt: Nova | ist | Mobilgerät
Merke dir: Regel: Mobilgerät | besitzt | Betriebssystem
Prüfe Wissen: Nova | besitzt | Betriebssystem
Korrigiere: Fakt: Nova | ist | Mobilgerät => Fakt: Nova | ist | Sensor
Widerrufe: Regel: Mobilgerät | besitzt | Betriebssystem
```

`Fakt` is one signed triple. `Regel: C | R | V` means every explicitly known member of C has R/V. `ist` is membership; a rule concluding `ist` permits another hop. `nicht R` is explicit negation. This is a small controlled language, not natural-language understanding, arbitrary first-order logic, or a planner. Facts are confirmed user assertions, not independently verified world truth. Output labels that distinction and lists content-hash source references and derivation steps.

The engine returns supported, refuted, conflict, unknown or limit. Missing facts are not false. Opposite literals conflict; a conflict in an intermediate premise taints its descendants. The engine conservatively abstains when its selected proof uses a conflict, even if an alternative clean proof might exist. Both opposing sources are shown. Corrections/revocations require exact old content and an Android confirmation; other facts are preserved.

`OnlineNaiveBayes` performs Laplace-smoothed incremental multinomial learning. It has separate predict/learn/evaluate/save/restore/reset functions. Production rebuilds the bounded derived counts from the existing approved command corpus, avoiding a second independently mutable command database. Unknown phrases may receive a **suggestion only**; no probabilistic output creates a `DEVICE_TOOL` decision. Exact approved commands still use the existing read-only ToolGate path. Scores are not calibrated probabilities; unknown vocabulary/weak scores abstain. A numerical boundary at 0.60 uses a 1e-12 tolerance.

## Integrated neural experiment

The learner is reachable directly from the chat and the existing Lernlabor button:

```
Neuron Demo
Neuron: Hallo
Neuron Status
Neuron lerne: Servus mein Assistent => Gruß
Neuron lerne: Wie lernst du dazu => Frage
Neuron zurücksetzen
```

Demo, teaching and reset each show an explicit confirmation. Training runs on `localAgentExecutor`; the existing Stop button requests cancellation. Cancelled/partial jobs do not publish weights. Existing custom lessons prevent silently rerunning the demo over them. Read-only predictions do not train anything. Reset touches only the experiment. Damaged persisted state is rejected rather than silently replaced; explicit experiment reset remains available.

The original Kotlin MLP has deterministic `java.util.Random(seed)` initialization, bounded inputs, 8 tanh hidden units, one binary output, numerically stable binary cross entropy and analytic backpropagation/SGD. The conversation experiment uses 32 hashed word features, 273 parameters and seed 42. It learns to distinguish greetings from questions; responses are explicitly labelled **prewritten**, not generated language. No claim of consciousness, autonomous intelligence or cloud-level ability is made. A separate 2-input nonlinear XOR experiment tests the same training implementation without increasing model complexity.

Snapshots contain weights, seed, update count and the approved corpus, are versioned/size-bounded/checksummed, and are stored under new keys in the existing SharedPreferences. Checksums detect corruption, not an attacker who can rewrite app-private storage. Existing fact/command/identity keys are retained. Content remains app-private, without new content encryption.

## Reproducible measurements and limits

Run `gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest` and `gradle :app:assembleDebug`. New tests are under `app/src/test/java/at/heinz/deviceai/learning/`. No new Gradle dependencies, pretrained weights or data assets are needed.

Local JVM check used OpenJDK 17, Kotlin compiler 2.0.21, JUnit 4.13.2 and an Android compile API jar for the unchanged command interpreter. This is NOT an Android device test or the project's Kotlin 2.4/Gradle build. 27 tests passed (9 existing bootstrap tests + 18 new tests). Initial new reasoning and integration assertions were observed failing on the previous behavior before implementation; absent new learner APIs initially failed compilation. No claim that every test individually followed a red/green cycle.

| Evaluation | Before | After | Data separation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Two-hop knowledge questions | 0/12 correct, 12 abstentions | 12/12 correct | Fresh object/category/resource names; no answer triples supplied |

The reasoning baseline was the actual `BootstrapBrain.kt` read from the pinned base snapshot, compiled alongside the new code under `OriginalBootstrapBrain`; only its object name and duplicate type declarations were changed. It was not simulated by a hand-written dummy baseline. Its existing `BootstrapTraining` dependency does not participate in the fact-only queries. Both the knowledge and suggestion comparisons proposed **zero** device commands. Zero wrong answers in these tiny positive fixtures is not an estimate of general error rate; contradiction, unknown, malformed, cancellation and corruption cases are covered separately.

Single warmed JVM run for 12 reasoning queries: old 2,976,392 ns / 137,840 allocated bytes; new 1,276,192 ns / 939,088 allocated bytes. These are one-run thread allocation and latency observations, not retained heap, peak RAM, Android battery measurements or a speedup claim. New inference allocates more because it builds proofs and source hashes. Neural greeting training took about 25–30 ms for 4000 updates on this host. Device measurements remain open. XOR snapshot: 320 bytes; dialogue snapshot after demo: 2566 bytes. New learning Kotlin sources: approximately 27 KB. APK delta must be measured from comparable CI artifacts; JVM class bytes are not a DEX/APK measurement.

Hard ceilings: 32 facts × 320 characters; 256 derived literals; 4096 rule checks; 16 derivation levels; bounded token/field input. Naive Bayes: 6 labels, 256 vocabulary terms, 256 examples, 32 tokens/example. Neural: input width 1–32, 8 hidden units, batches ≤128, steps ≤5000/call, wall limit ≤5 s (app uses 2 s), ≤100000 cumulative updates, 64 dialogue examples. Weights must be finite and bounded; malformed snapshots and oversized inputs are rejected. Finite-difference tests independently check every gradient on a small network. No new network, background service, tool permissions or identity mutations.

# Continuum Phase 1

Status: IMPLEMENTED AND CI VERIFIED on the direct Continuum stack as of 2026-10-13.

## What Phase 1 proves

Phase 1 establishes that Device AI can represent its persistent assistant identity separately from the currently loaded language model.

The implemented runtime now has four distinct layers:

```text
Signed Continuum Seed
        ↓
Content-addressed state root
        ↓
Cognitive archive / memory / experience
        ↓
Replaceable local model runtime
```

The local model is therefore no longer the sole carrier of the assistant's identity or long-term state.

## Implemented runtime

`ContinuumSeed.kt`
- typed instance, governance, state-format and model-ABI versions,
- authorized-node identifiers,
- current content-addressed state root,
- deterministic payload encoding,
- signature envelope,
- SHA-256 integrity,
- bounds and future-schema rejection.

`ContinuumSeedStore.kt`
- bounded primary + last-known-good seed persistence,
- atomic replacement,
- signature verification on load,
- fail-closed handling when stored seed state exists but is invalid.

`ContinuumState.kt`
- SHA-256 content-addressed object IDs,
- immutable object types,
- bounded file-backed object store,
- integrity checks and corruption rejection,
- provider-neutral replica-store interface.

`ContinuumRuntimeStore.kt`
- genesis creation,
- signed seed/state-root binding,
- cognitive archive hash binding,
- checkpoint generations,
- crash reconciliation using validated primary/LKG archive candidates,
- fail-closed behavior when the signed state root cannot be satisfied.

`AiContextCompiler.kt`
- identity/governance always precede lower-priority context,
- hybrid memory retrieval,
- privacy filtering,
- optional research evidence explicitly marked untrusted,
- registered tools and model capabilities,
- secret redaction and hard context byte budget.

`Deliberation.kt`
- FAST / STANDARD / DEEP / MULTI_CANDIDATE / VERIFY_ONLY / RESEARCH_BACKED / TOOL_PLAN,
- hard model-call, branch, critic, verifier, research, context, time and checkpoint budgets,
- cancellation,
- data-only Candidate/Critic/Verifier/Judge interfaces.

`ComputeFabric.kt`
- signed capability-manifest verification abstraction,
- typed node/task/result structures,
- least-privilege permissions,
- deadline/RAM/backend/output constraints,
- revocation and compatible-node scheduling,
- result hash/signature validation.

`CognitiveRaid.kt`
- SEED / CRITICAL / EVIDENCE / CACHE tiers,
- desired/required replica policy,
- health and reconstructibility assessment.

`ContinuumBenchmark.kt`
- fixed benchmark categories and aggregate metrics,
- model-mortality continuity fingerprint separated from model-specific output.

`AgentActivity.kt`
- opens or creates the Continuum runtime on startup,
- restores persisted memory and experience state,
- builds local-model context through `AiContextCompiler`,
- preserves ToolGate and registered-tool restrictions,
- checkpoints Continuum state after successful local turns.

## What Phase 1 does not prove

It does not prove:
- Astra/frontier-model parity,
- real Fold inference quality,
- real model-switch continuity on hardware,
- remote compute,

Phase 2 should turn the foundations into effective intelligence:

1. production Candidate/Critic/Judge execution through `LocalModelRuntime`,
2. task classifier + runtime strategy selection,

The user still experiences one assistant. Internal reasoning workers never become independent identities and never gain direct device-tool authority.

# Continuum Phase 2 — Effective Intelligence

Phase 2 turns the Phase 1 continuity substrate into measured problem-solving improvements.

The first implementation block adds:

- deterministic task classification,
- runtime selection of bounded reasoning strategy,
- data-only Candidate / Critic / Verifier / Judge coordination,
- an explicit internal-pass contract that has no ToolGate, DeviceToolExecutor or shell authority,
- proof-carrying append-only memory mutations signed by the identity signer,
- MemoryWritePolicy gating before a mutation can become durable,
- evaluated Experience -> typed SkillCandidate crystallization,
- owner approval remaining mandatory for skill promotion.

The purpose is not to claim frontier-model parity. The purpose is to build the mechanisms that can be benchmarked against the exact same local model in single-pass mode.

## Permanent boundaries

Internal reasoning passes may receive bounded context, emit text, be cancelled, and be evaluated.

They may not execute tools, request shell access as an executable action, alter governance, enroll compute nodes, contact the web implicitly, or mutate durable memory without a proof-carrying MemoryWritePolicy-approved transaction.

## Next integration step

After the Phase 2 foundation is CI-green, add a text-only adapter around LocalModelRuntime and expose a controlled DEEP mode. The same imported local model will then be benchmarked in:

1. single-pass baseline,
2. Continuum multi-pass mode.

Only measured differences may be reported as capability improvements.

# Kontrastives Lernen – experimentelle Verifikation

Der bestehende SWB1-Subword-Encoder wird ohne externe Gewichte genutzt. Der Experimentpfad trainiert ausschließlich eine Kopie und ersetzt weder produktive Modellgewichte noch Benutzererinnerungen automatisch.

## Prüfungen

* Positive Textpaare entstehen durch maskierte Wortansichten, negative durch verschiedene Trainingsbeispiele.
* Training und Validierung nutzen getrennte, normalisierte Texte. Die Testdaten sind synthetisch und enthalten keine privaten Informationen.
* Die CI führt Node → Kotlin → Node aus: Node erstellt eine SWB1-Referenz und Evaluationskennzahlen, Kotlin trainiert unabhängig, vergleicht 4.113 Modellparameter sowie Top-1/MRR-Kennzahlen mit einer absoluten Toleranz von 1e-8 und schreibt den eigenen Modellstand; Node prüft diesen erneut.
* Änderungen an den Modellgewichten dürfen nicht als allgemeine Intelligenzsteigerung ausgegeben werden. Die unabhängige Holdout-Kennzahl wird dokumentiert, nicht automatisch als Erfolg gewertet.
* Vor einer produktiven Aktivierung fehlen zusätzliche, disjunkte Datensätze, eine belastbare Regressionsgrenze, Stabilitätsprüfungen und die kontrollierte Übernahme in ContinuumLearningCore.

Die täglichen Offline-Jobs können vom Android-Betriebssystem verschoben werden. Die Fehlerprotokollierung verhindert stilles Verschlucken von Ausnahmen; sie garantiert kein permanentes Hintergrundtraining.

# Bounded Deep Research Engine

## Architecture and state machine

`DeepResearchEngine` is a provider-neutral read-only pipeline layered on `ResearchProvider`,
`SourceTrustStore`, `Claim`, and `MemoryWritePolicy`:

`PLAN → DISCOVERY → FETCH → EXTRACT → GRAPH → GAP_ANALYSIS → FOLLOW_UP → SYNTHESIZE → COMPLETE`

Failures or unavailable discovery produce `PARTIAL`; cooperative cancellation is checked between
queries and fetches. `ResearchRound` records bounded round/query/source metadata. The planner
interface accepts a future local-model adapter through `ResearchPlanGenerator`; the current app
uses deterministic question splitting and requires an explicit Web/QUICK, STANDARD, or DEEP
selection. Ordinary LOCAL/AUTO chat never invokes research implicitly.

## Hard budgets

Every mode resolves to fixed app-owned limits. A planner cannot change a mode's budget; paths
and follow-ups are truncated to the validated policy. HTTP requests carry the per-source byte,
request timeout, and redirect limits; an overall monotonic deadline, source/claim caps, and
per-domain fan-out are checked by the engine.

| Mode | Discovery paths | Rounds | Sources | Bytes/source | Total bytes | Claims | Request / deadline | Counter / follow-up |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| QUICK | 2 | 1 | 3 | 64 KB | 128 KB | 32 | 5 s / 15 s | 0 / 0 |
| STANDARD | 5 | 2 | 8 | 128 KB | 512 KB | 96 | 8 s / 45 s | 2 / 3 |
| DEEP | 10 | 3 | 16 | 256 KB | 1.5 MB | 192 | 10 s / 90 s | 8 / 8 |

All limits have additional absolute constructor ceilings. Redirects are limited to 1, 3, and 4
by mode respectively; per-domain fan-out is at most two sources.

## Discovery, sources, and trust

Discovery is separate from known-URL retrieval. The production UI currently configures no
general search provider and does not use a cloud search API or credential. Operators can include
direct HTTPS seed URLs; without seeds, the UI and dossier say that general discovery is
unavailable rather than claiming web search occurred. Candidate and redirected URLs pass the
existing HTTPS/SSRF validator, canonicalization, credential-query rejection, and per-domain
limits before source acceptance.

Canonical URLs discard fragments and common tracking parameters. Exact content hashes and a
deterministic near-duplicate grouping identify mirrors; a duplicate is not an independent
corroborating source. Dossier source metadata retains URL/domain, retrieval time, content hash,
bounded snippet, and extracted version/date applicability where present.

The evidence graph keeps claim nodes, source links, claim-to-claim SUPPORTS/CONTRADICTS edges,
source DUPLICATE_MIRROR/UNKNOWN relations, a coverage score, and independent-source count.
These lexical support scores are explainable heuristics, not calibrated probabilities. Source
trust snapshots distinguish evaluated profiles from unknown defaults and expose historical
authority, query relevance, freshness, corroboration, and duplicate penalty. Domain count alone
does not establish trust.

## Gaps, falsification, and synthesis boundary

After extraction, missing subquestion coverage and contradictions become explicit gaps. STANDARD
and DEEP can use the bounded follow-up wave when a general discovery provider exists. DEEP adds a
counter-evidence path and preserves contradiction edges instead of majority-voting them away.
With no configured discovery provider, direct seed research remains available; a second wave
cannot invent additional URLs.

Fetched page text is hostile evidence. `ResearchPromptBoundary` puts bounded source excerpts in
quoted untrusted-data sections, escapes role labels and delimiters, and expressly denies them
authority to request tools/actions, change budgets, or rewrite policy. Synthesis is a
provider-neutral text-only interface. The Android adapter uses the ready local LiteRT-LM model;
any generated structured tool proposal is discarded, never passed to ToolGate or an executor.
Actual citations are appended from the retrieved dossier, not invented by the model.

## Persistence, resume, and memory

`FileResearchDossierStore` uses explicit typed binary fields, schema versioning, a SHA-256
integrity envelope, a 1 MB cap, and atomic replacement. Malformed, oversized, tampered, and
unsupported-schema records fail closed. Checkpoints preserve the phase, completed URLs/content
hashes, and byte count. Partial dossiers preserve bounded source snippets. Resume requires a
matching, non-stale checkpoint/dossier pair and skips already completed canonical URLs; it may
re-extract from bounded stored snippets, so no claim is made that it retains full downloaded
pages. Dossiers are classified PRIVATE by `MemoryWritePolicy` because they contain user-provided
research queries.

Web claims are not automatically promoted to long-term memory. `storeValidatedKnowledge` writes
only claims that are independently verified, have at least two independent sources, are
explicitly selected for storage, and pass `MemoryWritePolicy`.

## Android path and validation boundary

The AgentActivity Web action explicitly arms exactly one QUICK/STANDARD/DEEP request. It displays
planning, fetching, checking, follow-up, synthesis, done, or partial state; cancellation is
cooperative between bounded provider operations. Research stays read-only and does not affect
ordinary local-first chat. A ready local model synthesizes evidence; otherwise a deterministic
summary is used and disclosed.

GitHub Actions run `38341592364` passed backend syntax, `:app:testDebugUnitTest`,
`:app:assembleDebug`, and upload of `DeviceAI-v0.3-debug-apk` (artifact `11787331710`) on the
pre-research head `adf399432dd43c4c37e39ac633d0eb58ee35dc71`. New research changes still need a
fresh CI run. Run `38349576117` for research commit `1550c53346e8f375f9d9948eb2098b74104310f6`
ended `action_required` with zero jobs; repository workflow approval is required. The sandbox
cannot resolve Android Gradle Plugin 8.10.0. The new engine's
standalone Kotlin compile and deterministic JVM tests are locally exercised with temporary
API/JUnit stubs, but this is not a substitute for Android Gradle CI. No live network, imported
model, physical-device inference, Fold layout, or on-device cancellation behavior has been
verified.

# Continuum Developer Agent

Deterministic, zero-cost repair agent for this repository. No LLM, no paid API, no
external service besides GitHub Actions itself. It **proposes** changes as draft
pull requests; it never merges and never pushes to a development or default branch.

## Repair loop (one session)

```
failure detected ─▶ reproduce (own check run) ─▶ diagnose ─▶ propose candidates
   ─▶ critic ─▶ apply in isolated git worktree ─▶ run fixed check chain
   ─▶ VERIFIED? ── yes ─▶ patch + report ─▶ (publish job) branch continuum-agent/* + draft PR
        └─ no ─▶ reset worktree, next candidate (budget: 4 tests, 2 per strategy, deadline)
   VERIFIED = every check of the chain passed AND tests were really executed
   (not skipped, not file placeholders) AND no fewer tests ran than passed in the
   failing baseline; a green exit code without that evidence is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
   ─▶ every attempt is written to the repair ledger (experience)
```

| Role | Module | What it really does |
|---|---|---|
| Diagnostician | `.github/continuum/repair-diagnostics.mjs` | Parses the agent's **own** reproduction run: Kotlin K1/K2 `e:` diagnostics, JUnit XML (Gradle and `node --test`), Node module-load errors from TAP. JS error headers are recognized structurally across Node releases (`ReferenceError: …`, `ReferenceError [Error]: …` of Node 20.20/22.16, `Uncaught …`, nested `[cause]:`, TAP YAML `name:`/`stack:`), each error only with frames of its **own** stack; generic `Error`/`AssertionError` text never becomes a code diagnostic. Real reporter output of Node 20.20.0, 22.16.0 and 22.22.0 is kept as fixtures in `fixtures/node-reporter/`. Counts total/failed/skipped/file placeholders/executed/passed tests. Paths outside the tree are dropped. Problem identity = fingerprint without line numbers. |
| Solution developer + code generator | `repair-strategies.mjs` | Deterministic strategies producing minimal unique hunks: `KOTLIN_ESCAPED_NEWLINE`, `KOTLIN_KNOWN_FIX:*` (rules in `repair-engine.mjs`), `KOTLIN_MISSING_IMPORT` (symbol index + JDK/Android table), `KOTLIN_TYPO_REFERENCE` (Damerau–Levenshtein over lexer identifiers), `KOTLIN_NULLABLE_STRING_DEFAULT`, `JS_MISSING_IMPORT`, `JS_TYPO_REFERENCE`, `REVERT_HUNK_TO_PARENT` (regression culprit search: undo one hunk of the failing commit, closest to a diagnostic first, so unrelated changes in the same file survive; review required), `REVERT_FILE_TO_PARENT` (fallback, review required), `EXPERIENCE_REPLAY` (re-apply a hunk verified for the same fingerprint). |
| Critic | `repair-critic.mjs` | Rejects before any test: workflows, Gradle files, manifest, signing material, consent/ToolGate/identity/credential files, the agent's own code, test sources (tests are the specification; only the syntax-only newline repair may touch them), >3 files, >40 changed lines, removed assertions, new `!!`, process execution, `eval`, `@Ignore`/`skip`, URLs, swallowed exceptions. |
| Test verifier | `repair-loop.mjs` | `git worktree add --detach` at the failing commit; fixed check chains only (`node`: `node --test` on `.github/continuum/*.test.mjs`; `android`: `gradle :app:compileDebugUnitTestKotlin` then `:app:testDebugUnitTest`; `jvm`: local JVM harness). Kotlin incremental compilation is disabled because its caches produced phantom errors after failed builds. Nested repair sessions are refused. |
| Experience learning | `repair-ledger.mjs` (+ `repair-experience.mjs`) | Every attempt with diagnosis, strategy, hunks, test outcome, base commit, patch SHA-256, confidence, branch/PR. Strategy statistics per `"<diagnostic kind>\|<strategy>"` rank future candidates (Laplace); candidates proven to fail for a fingerprint are never retried; verified hunks are replayed. Persisted on branch `continuum-agent-state` with stale-write protection. |
| Publisher | `repair-publish.mjs` | Runs in a job **without build execution** and with the write token. Re-validates patch hash, critic verdict, that every check of the chain passed and that the evidence rests on executed tests (flags in the report alone are not trusted), `git apply`s onto the exact base, pushes only `continuum-agent/*`, opens a **draft** PR. If Actions may not create PRs, records the HTTP status and a compare link instead. |
| Orchestrator / CLI | `developer-agent.mjs` | `triage`, `repair`, `benchmark`, `watch`, `publish`, `publish-demo`, `ledger-save`, `backlog …`, `backlog-save`. |
| Development backlog | `development-backlog.mjs`, `development-planner.mjs`, `backlog-cli.mjs` | Persistent tasks shared with the Android app (same rules in `DevelopmentBacklog.kt`): analyzer findings become proposals, every real repair session is recorded on its REPAIR task with the evidence that verified it; DONE only with executed-test evidence. See `docs/DEVELOPMENT_BACKLOG.md`. |
| Structural analysis | `code-analyzer.mjs`, `kotlin-tokenizer.mjs` | Lexer-based symbol index, import/package resolution, reachability from AndroidManifest components, `UNREFERENCED`/`TEST_ONLY`/`DEAD_CLUSTER` findings with confidence, `--chain A B` call chains. Name-based member resolution is an over-approximation: findings are evidence, not proof. |

## Triggers

* **Failed Android build on `copilot/**`** → `android.yml` jobs `repair` (read-only) and `publish-repair` (write). Works on the development branch today.
* **Push of agent code** → `continuum-developer-agent.yml` job `agent`: all agent tests, structural analysis, CI triage and the JavaScript fault-injection benchmark through the real loop.
* **Manual** (`workflow_dispatch`, or a push to the development branch whose head commit message contains `[agent-kotlin-benchmark]` / `[agent-publish-demo]`): `kotlin_benchmark` runs the Kotlin faults through the real Android Gradle chain; `publish_demo` pushes one verified benchmark repair as `continuum-agent/demo/<run>/fault-*` + `.../repair-*` and opens a draft PR repair → fault (never into a real branch).
* **Hourly** (`cron: 23 * * * *`, job `watch`): API-only check of the development head; the heavy Android repair job starts only if the head's Android build failed and no session for that commit exists in the ledger.

### Activating the hourly schedule

GitHub evaluates `schedule` **only from the default branch**. The cron line in the
development branch therefore has no effect until the owner places this workflow
file on `main` (copy or merge of `.github/workflows/continuum-developer-agent.yml`;
the workflow checks out the development branch for all agent code). The agent does
not push to `main` itself.

Minutes: the repository is private. The hourly `watch` job is API-only (≈1 billed
minute per run, ≈720 per month); Android repairs only run for red, unrepaired heads.

### Allowing draft pull requests

Creating PRs with `GITHUB_TOKEN` requires *Settings → Actions → General → Workflow
permissions → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"*. Without
it the agent still pushes the verified branch and stores a compare link
(`pullRequest.status = NOT_PERMITTED`). Note: branches pushed and PRs opened with
`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other workflows; the verification evidence is the
agent's own isolated test run recorded in the PR body and ledger.

## Fault-injection benchmark (acceptance check)

`node .github/continuum/developer-agent.mjs benchmark --chains node=node,kotlin=android --out <dir>`

Each fault is an exact edit committed on top of HEAD in an isolated worktree; the
agent is not told the fault. Catalog (`repair-benchmark.mjs`):

| Fault | Origin | Expected repair |
|---|---|---|
| `js-typo-reference` | synthetic | `JS_TYPO_REFERENCE` |
| `js-missing-import` | synthetic | `JS_MISSING_IMPORT` |
| `js-masked-missing-import` | synthetic; the `ReferenceError` is swallowed by a `try/catch` | `REVERT_FILE_TO_PARENT` (only visible as wrong behavior) |
| `kt-historical-escaped-newline-48bd150` | **real CI failure** of head 48bd150 | `KOTLIN_ESCAPED_NEWLINE` |
| `kt-historical-set-takelast-373bddb` | **real CI failure** fixed by 373bddb | `KOTLIN_KNOWN_FIX:SET_TAKELAST` or revert |
| `kt-typo-reference` | synthetic | `KOTLIN_TYPO_REFERENCE` |
| `kt-missing-import` | synthetic | `KOTLIN_MISSING_IMPORT` |
| `kt-behavior-regression` | synthetic; duplicate-key check removed, unit test fails | `REVERT_FILE_TO_PARENT` |

## Honest limits

* No code model is used. The agent repairs **diagnosable, local** defects
  (syntax, references, imports, known rules) and finds regressions by reverting
  single hunks, then whole files, of the failing commit. It does not understand intent and
  cannot implement features or fix logic errors that are not regressions.
* A green check proves only what the tests check. Every proposal stays a draft
  and needs human review; every `REVERT_*` repair is marked review-required.
* Research direction (not implemented): a small local code model ranking or
  generating candidates, trained on the ledger's verified hunks. The ledger format
  already stores the needed (diagnostic, before, after, outcome) tuples.
