# Persistent development backlog (Node ↔ Kotlin)

One backlog format and one set of state rules for every writer: the Node developer
agent and CLI (`.github/continuum/development-backlog.mjs`) and the Android app
(`app/src/main/java/at/heinz/deviceai/cognitive/DevelopmentBacklog.kt` +
`DevelopmentBacklogStore.kt`). It extends the existing development pipeline:
`code-analyzer` findings (ranked by `development-planner.mjs`) and repair-loop
sessions become backlog tasks, and Android `DevelopmentCoordinator` jobs are
recorded as backlog tasks instead of being lost on restart.

## Document

* Canonical JSON: object keys sorted (UTF-16 order), no whitespace, **integers
  only** (|n| ≤ 2^53−1; floats are rejected because JS and the JVM print them
  differently), strings escaped exactly like `JSON.stringify`, UTF-8 without BOM,
  one trailing newline. Same state ⇒ same bytes on both platforms.
* `integrity` = SHA-256 of the canonical document without that field. It detects
  corruption and partial writes. **It is not a signature** and proves nothing
  about who wrote the file.
* Strict reading on both sides: invalid UTF-8, BOM, duplicate keys, floats, lone
  surrogates, trailing data, unknown states, dependency cycles, unsorted tasks
  ⇒ `CORRUPT`; hash mismatch ⇒ `INTEGRITY_MISMATCH`; `schemaVersion` > 2 ⇒
  `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` (never overwritten, never "recovered" away).
* Unknown fields (top level and inside tasks) are preserved through every
  operation and rewrite (forward compatibility).
* `schemaVersion` 1 (the earlier `development-planner` snapshot) is migrated
  explicitly: every finding becomes a `PROPOSED` `INVESTIGATE` task with a
  deterministic id `inv-<sha256(kind,file,symbol)[0:16]>`; all planner fields are
  kept in `subject`/`migratedFrom`; the original file is kept as `<file>.v1.json`.

## Task states

```
PROPOSED ─accept─▶ READY ─claim/claimNext─▶ IN_PROGRESS ─submit─▶ VERIFYING ─complete(evidence)─▶ DONE
    │                │  ▲                      │    │                  │
    │                │  └── fail / expire ─────┘    └── fail ──────────┤ (attempts < maxAttempts)
    │                │                         FAILED ◀── fail/expire ─┘ (budget exhausted) ─retry─▶ READY
    │                └─ (dependency FAILED/ABORTED/REJECTED) ⇄ BLOCKED      (automatic)
    └─reject─▶ REJECTED        any non-terminal ─abort─▶ ABORTED          DONE/ABORTED/REJECTED are final
```

| Operation | Rule |
|---|---|
| `propose` | new id (`[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,63}`), title 1..200 chars without control characters, dependencies must exist; `ifAbsent` makes re-proposing idempotent |
| `claim` / `claimNext` | only `READY`, all dependencies `DONE`, `attempts < maxAttempts`; sets a lease (1 min .. 24 h) and a 32-hex token; `claimNext` = highest priority, then oldest, then id; optional `kinds` filter |
| `renew` / `submit` | only with the claim token and before the lease ends; `submit` records the artifact (`PATCH`/`PROPOSAL`/`REPORT` + SHA-256) |
| `complete` | only `VERIFYING`, only with evidence that names the task, the submission token and the submitted artifact hash, is not older than the submission, has every check passed (`failed = 0`), at least one executed test, and `executed > 0` for every test profile (`node-continuum`, `android-unit`, `jvm-harness`) |
| `fail` | with the claim or submission token; back to `READY` while budget remains, otherwise `FAILED`; optional (failing) evidence is kept |
| `expire` | every `IN_PROGRESS` task whose lease ended returns to `READY`/`FAILED` with `LEASE_EXPIRED` (crash recovery, resumable work) |
| `retry` | `FAILED` → `READY`, budget reset (a human decision) |
| `reject` / `abort` / `setPriority` | explicit reasons; terminal tasks cannot change |
| any operation with `opId` | applied at most once: the last 256 applied ids are kept in `recentOpIds`; a repeated id is a reported no-op (`duplicate`). This makes operation logs (CI re-runs, re-imported exports from the phone) exactly-once within that window |

The DONE rule is enforced **twice**: by the `complete` operation and on every
load (a file whose DONE task lacks matching evidence is `CORRUPT`). History is
bounded to 40 entries and evidence to 8 per task; drops are counted
(`historyDropped`, `evidenceDropped`), never silent. Every rejected operation
returns a stable error code (`INVALID_TRANSITION`, `TOKEN_MISMATCH`,
`LEASE_EXPIRED`, `EVIDENCE_REJECTED`, `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `DEPENDENCY_NOT_DONE`,
`NO_ELIGIBLE_TASK`, `DUPLICATE_ID`, `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY`, `NOT_FOUND`,
`INVALID_FIELD`, `INVALID_OP`, `LIMIT`).

## Store guarantees (both platforms)

* Cross-process lock `<file>.lock` (exclusive create). A lock older than 60 s is
  moved aside under a unique name and broken; if what was moved turns out to be
  fresh it is put back. Waiting is bounded (`LOCK_TIMEOUT`).
* Read-modify-write is a compare-and-swap: before the rename the file must still
  hold the bytes that were read, else `CONFLICT` and nothing is written; callers
  may also pass `expectedRevision`.
* Atomic replace: synced temp file + rename (+ directory sync where supported).
  The previous version is kept as `<file>.bak`. An interrupted write leaves only
  a temp file, which is never read and is removed later.
* A corrupt file is recovered from `<file>.bak` and quarantined as
  `<file>.corrupt-*` (reported in the result), never deleted; without a valid
  backup loading fails closed.
* Batches are all-or-nothing by default; the lenient mode reports every rejected
  operation with its code.

## Who writes what

| Writer | How |
|---|---|
| Analyzer findings | `syncBacklogOps` (`development-planner.mjs`): new `DEAD_CLUSTER`/`TEST_ONLY`/`UNREFERENCED` findings become `PROPOSED` `INVESTIGATE` tasks (at most 12 new per run, highest priority first); vanished findings withdraw only untouched proposals; accepted, rejected or aborted tasks are never changed by the planner |
| Repair loop | `repairSessionOps`: one `REPAIR` task per failure identity (`rep-` + hash of chain and diagnostic fingerprints); a session is recorded as propose → accept → claim → submit (patch hash) → complete with the evidence of the very tests that verified the patch, or → fail. Every step has an `opId`, so recording a session twice changes nothing. A task that is DONE, FAILED (budget), REJECTED or ABORTED is not touched, and `publish` opens no further draft PR for it |
| CI | `backlog-save` (publish jobs, write token) on branch `continuum-agent-state`: `expire`, repair sessions, planner sync; compare-and-swap on the branch head. `watch` reads ledger and backlog through the API and fails instead of assuming empty state when they are unreadable |
| Humans / other agents | `node .github/continuum/developer-agent.mjs backlog show|plan|accept|reject|abort|retry|priority|claim|renew|submit|verify|fail|expire|apply --file <backlog.json>`; `verify` is the only producer of test evidence: it checks that the patch is the submitted artifact (SHA-256), applies it to `--base` in an isolated worktree and runs a fixed check chain |
| Android app | `DevelopmentBacklogStore` in app storage; see `AgentActivity` (development backlog) |

## Verification

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Shared conformance vectors (every operation and error code, bounded history/evidence) | `app/src/test/resources/continuum/backlog/conformance.json`, run by `development-backlog.test.mjs` and `DevelopmentBacklogTest.kt` |
| Byte-identical encoding, invalid documents, v1 migration | same fixture directory (`valid-v2.json`, `unknown-fields.json`, `invalid*.json`, `v1-*.json`) |
| Store: backup, quarantine, fail-closed, CAS conflicts, stale/fresh locks, interrupted writes | both test suites |
| Concurrency without lost updates | 5 Node writer **processes**; 6 Kotlin writer threads with separate stores |
| Real cross-runtime round trip | CI (`android.yml`): `backlog-fixtures.mjs roundtrip-prepare` (Node writes) → `DevelopmentBacklogRoundtripTest` inside `:app:testDebugUnitTest` (Kotlin verifies, changes through its store, writes an operation log) → `roundtrip-verify` (Node checks bytes, revision, states, unknown fields, UTF-8, no lock/temp leftovers, applies the Kotlin operation log) |

Regenerate fixtures only after an intentional rule or format change:
`node .github/continuum/backlog-fixtures.mjs write` (the Node test fails while
committed fixtures are stale; the Kotlin test then checks the new expectations).

## Honest limits

* The integrity hash is not authentication. Anyone who can write the file can
  forge a consistent document, including evidence; trust comes from where the
  file lives (the agent state branch is written only by the CI publish job).
* File locks are advisory. Mutual exclusion holds unless a holder exceeds the
  60 s stale threshold; the compare-and-swap then turns a lost race into an
  explicit `CONFLICT` instead of a lost update (the remaining window is the
  instant between the final check and the rename).
* Evidence produced on Android is impossible by design: the app cannot run the
  test suites, so app-side work stops at `VERIFYING` until CI or a developer
  records real test evidence.

# In-app development proposals (PR #19)

The user sees one assistant. Developer, Critic, TestDesigner and Judge are internal, sequential, data-only roles using the existing LocalModelReasoningAdapter. No cloud fallback or worker tool authority exists.

## Review contract

All reviewers receive the selected source snapshots and complete developer output, including replacements. TestDesigner also receives the critic output; Judge receives complete critic and test-design output. Prompt size and cumulative UTF-8 limits remain mandatory: a larger context fails explicitly rather than being clipped. A Judge recommendation conflicting with REVISE, REJECT, BLOCKER findings or empty edits fails closed. A rejected review may still be displayed as a rejected, read-only report. Model approval never grants execution authority.

## Source selection

The first UI slice accepts at most four selected sources, totaling 4,000 UTF-8 bytes by default. Selection now rejects excess content immediately. SAF document display names are snapshot labels, NOT proof of repository location. Their SHA-256 identifies the selected content only, not current GitHub state. There is no apply/push capability. Before any future apply feature, add explicit owner-confirmed repository-relative path mapping and revalidate the live destination hash. Duplicate labels are rejected. Source text remains untrusted evidence.

Changed goals/sources invalidate old proposal export. Launching an asynchronous SAF source read now immediately revokes any previous proposal, blocks Start and repeated imports until the read finishes, and keeps old sources available if the picker yields nothing. The UI provides a clear-selection action, and rejects more than four selected URIs explicitly instead of silently ignoring some. SAF reads are capped at the same 4,000-byte limit enforced by the controller. Active jobs copy the source list. Cancellation is checked again after state notifications and after model calls; elapsed monotonic time bounds the job even if wall-clock time moves backward.

## Verification

Run the real project tasks: `gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest --stacktrace` and `gradle :app:assembleDebug --stacktrace`. The existing android.yml push trigger matches the PR branch; it uploads DeviceAI-v0.3-debug-apk and fails if the APK is missing. A successful standalone stub harness is not a substitute for these tasks. No successful CI/build/device result is claimed by this document. Record the exact tested head and inspect checks after the commit.

DevelopmentReviewRegressionTest includes a scripted increment correction, full review-context checks, conflicting verdicts, empty edits, callback cancellation, wall-clock rollback, mutable inputs, source byte limits and stale exports. These are scripted fakes, not a model-quality benchmark; suggested tests in a proposal are NOT EXECUTED.

## Real-model smoke test (after verified APK)

1. Install the verified PR APK without merging main. Load an owner-selected compatible local model.
2. Open Entwicklungsaufgabe. Select a small Counter.kt containing `fun increment(value: Int): Int = value - 1`.
3. Request: Correct increment(1) to return 2 and suggest a regression test. Start.
4. Record model ID, app commit, role progression, elapsed time, call count, final decision, actual replacement and suggested tests. Do not treat the suggestion as executed.
5. Repeat a cancellation test; inspect visible terminal status. Check that no source was modified.

## Still requires verification

Baseline PR #19 head `e12693ffa41bcb8f9096cb57654901535691263e` passed actual `:app:testDebugUnitTest`, `:app:assembleDebug` and APK upload in workflow run `38376951781`. This is evidence for that head only; inspect a fresh run after further commits. PR descriptions and scripted demonstrations are not test evidence.

The Activity's SAF import maps display names only and caps read size separately; oversized selections are rejected by the controller. Restart recovery is unavailable; jobs are not persisted. Applying edits, running generated tests, building/installing APKs or pushing changes from the in-app bots are absent by design. Any future execution requires typed least-privilege owner-authorized capabilities behind ToolGate.

# Identity and Self Model (Part 2)

This describes **identity representation** (persistent, versioned state). It is not consciousness, sentience or
self-awareness; nothing here claims the system has any of these.

## Hash vs. signature
`integrityHash` (SHA-256 over a deterministic canonical form) detects tampering. It does not authenticate the author.
Cryptographic signatures (e.g. Android Keystore) are planned, not implemented.

## BehaviorProfile
Eleven typed traits (`BehaviorTrait`), each 0..1, all start at 0.5 (neutral). Immutable; `with()` rejects NaN/Infinity/out-of-range.
Genome `BehaviorBounds` (default 0.05..0.95) are enforced by policy and validator.

## BehaviorEvidence / Proposal / Policy / History
A `BehaviorProposal` carries a trait, proposed value, reason and `BehaviorEvidence` (id, strength 0..1, measuredOutcome -1..1).
`BehaviorUpdatePolicy`: `step = learningRate * meanStrength * meanOutcome`, limited to `maxBehaviorStep` (0.05), never
overshooting the proposed value, clamped to bounds. Rejected when evidence is missing/duplicate/weak, for the wrong trait,
non-finite, or pointing in the opposite direction. One update can therefore never move 0.5 to 1.0.
Accepted changes are recorded in the append-only `BehaviorHistory` as `BehaviorChange` (previous, proposed, accepted, evidence ids,
strength, outcome, reason, timestamp, source and resulting generation).

## SelfModel and CapabilityEvidence
Ten `Capability` domains, each a `CapabilityEstimate` (competence, calibrationError, evaluatedTaskCount, knownLimitations).
Initially uncertain: competence 0.5, 0 tasks, confidence 0. Each `CapabilityEvidence` (task, predicted confidence, actual score,
evaluator, timestamp) moves competence and calibrationError by the genome's selfModel rate (0.1, an exponential moving average).
`confidence = 1 - calibrationError` once evaluated: repeated overconfidence raises calibrationError and lowers confidence;
accurate predictions improve it. Confidence is not certainty. `SelfModel.explain(capability)` returns the supporting evidence.

## IdentityDrift
Deterministic continuity metric between two states: 0.5*behavior + 0.3*capability(competence) + 0.2*communication drift.
Ignores memory/experience roots and session data. Allowed range: `UpdateLimits.maxDriftPerGeneration` (0.1).

## IdentityUpdateValidator
Returns `Valid` or `Invalid(failures)` with codes: INVALID_NUMBER, OUT_OF_BOUNDS, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, EVIDENCE_MISMATCH,
IDENTITY_MISMATCH, BROKEN_ANCESTRY, GENOME_MISMATCH, EXCESSIVE_DRIFT, FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITY, INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

## Generation lifecycle
Generation N -> proposal -> policy -> validator -> Generation N+1 (`AdaptiveIdentity`). Rejections change nothing; old
generations are never modified; `IdentityHistory.audit()` verifies the chain.

## Safety
Genome flags allowSelfReplication / allowHiddenPersistence / allowShutdownEvasion cannot be set true.

# Android installation and signing (Device AI 0.3.1)

The regular debug APK uses `applicationId=at.heinz.deviceai`. The GitHub Actions runner may create a fresh debug signing key; Android then refuses an in-place update of an already installed APK signed by a different key (`INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`). Increasing versionCode cannot bypass a signature mismatch.

For testing without removing the installed app or losing its data, the same CI workflow also builds an isolated **Device AI Preview** APK with package `at.heinz.deviceai.preview` and a different visible app label. Install the preview alongside the existing app. **Preview app data and permissions are independent** (including Shizuku authorization, imported models and settings). Do not assume settings are migrated.

Both APK variants are debug-signed, not distribution releases. An update of either package in later workflow runs will likewise require a stable signing key. Production upgrades must use a securely stored signing keystore provided through CI secrets; do not commit private signing keys or use a publicly derivable signing key. Until stable signing is configured, prefer preview for initial side-by-side testing, and retain old installations when their data matters.

GitHub Actions runs actual `gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest`, `gradle :app:assembleDebug`, and `gradle :app:clean :app:assembleDebug -PdeviceAiPreview=true`. The preview and regular APKs must each be downloaded from their corresponding artifact. Successful builds do not establish installation success on a physical Samsung Fold.

FILE 346/375: docs/LOCAL_FIRST_PROTOTYPE.md
SHA-256: 5b405899ba35894006d298f5c133014f1cfe5f9e2b4df8bb061e7077323ab13d

# Local-first prototype

## Working path

AgentActivity AUTO and LOCAL use an imported LiteRT-LM model when its runtime is READY.
Input is assembled with the bounded local memory retrieval and passed to
`BoundedAgentOrchestrator`. The runtime receives only function schemas derived from
`ToolRegistry`; generated function calls become validated `ToolProposal` objects. They
never execute as model-provided shell text.

The orchestrator records proposals and delegates to `ToolGate`. Read-only tools are enabled
by the app's explicit local policy. CONFIRM tools show a confirmation dialog; DESTRUCTIVE
tools require a second, stronger confirmation. Denials return as tool observations. Approved
calls go through `DeviceToolExecutor` and Shizuku. Bounded results and denials return through
LiteRT-LM `Content.ToolResponse` messages before the model generates its final answer.
Responses are evaluated and stored as in-memory `Experience`; memory writes require an
explicit remember request and pass `MemoryWritePolicy`.

The expert interpreter in MainActivity is a separate USER-ONLY screen. It is not registered
as a tool, and `ToolProposal` rejects shell names and command-like arguments.

## Model import

Use **MODELL IMPORTIEREN** and select a `.litertlm` file through Android's document picker.
The operator supplies a model id, version and expected SHA-256. The app copies the document
to its private catalog, checks the digest and inspects capabilities before accepting it.
Only text models with CPU support are eligible. CPU is the supported baseline; GPU/NPU
capabilities are displayed only when model inspection reports them. No weights are bundled
or downloaded. Import can fail when model/runtime/device compatibility is unknown.

The UI distinguishes NO MODEL, INSTALLED, READY, LOADING, GENERATING, ERROR and OFFLINE
(the selected local-only mode). Generation waits are capped at 120 seconds; model import,
load and unload surface a 120-second UI timeout. Native work or a blocked document provider
may continue after that UI timeout, so the screen reports ERROR instead of claiming the
operation was forcibly stopped. The UI displays model id, version, inspected capabilities
and backend support. OFFLINE means the local-only route does not contact the cloud; it is not
a claim about the device's network connectivity.

## Replay and side-effect guarantee

Tool receipts are stored locally in a bounded, versioned file with atomic replacement and
checksum verification. Raw argument strings and tool output are not stored; argument values
are sanitized and outputs are represented by bounded length and hash metadata. A prior
SUCCEEDED call id is returned as already completed. A STARTED call id is blocked; FAILED,
TIMED_OUT and CANCELLED call ids are terminal and never retried. On startup, receipts in
these potentially ambiguous states are shown in a review dialog without exposing raw arguments
or output.

This is durable replay suppression, not universal exactly-once execution. Android/Shizuku
side effects cannot be rolled back or reliably terminated after process death. If a process
dies after STARTED and before a terminal receipt is durable, the outcome may be unknown and
the call is blocked rather than blindly retried.

## Validation boundary

GitHub Actions run `38341592364` passed backend syntax, `:app:testDebugUnitTest`,
`:app:assembleDebug`, and uploaded `DeviceAI-v0.3-debug-apk` (artifact `11787331710`) for
commit `adf399432dd43c4c37e39ac633d0eb58ee35dc71`. It predates the Deep Research changes in
this branch and does not validate them. A fresh green run/artifact is still required. This
sandbox could not resolve Android Gradle Plugin 8.10.0, so its Gradle test/build tasks could
not run locally.
The research-head workflow run `38349576117` ended `action_required` with zero jobs, so it
produced neither test/build results nor an APK; repository workflow approval is required.

No physical-device inference is claimed. Importing and running a real model, native runtime
compatibility, tool behavior through Shizuku, cancellation behavior, performance/thermal
limits, and Fold-device layout still require physical Fold testing.

## Explicit Deep Research

Web access is opt-in through the **Web** action and a QUICK, STANDARD, or DEEP selection.
Normal LOCAL/AUTO chat never triggers it implicitly. Research is read-only, uses HTTPS seed
URLs supplied in the prompt, and clearly reports that general web discovery is not configured.
A ready LiteRT-LM model may synthesize bounded evidence; model-generated tool proposals are
discarded in this path. See [`DEEP_RESEARCH_ENGINE.md`](DEEP_RESEARCH_ENGINE.md) for budgets,
claim/evidence graphs, trust, injection boundaries, persistence and resume behavior.

FILE 347/375: docs/LOCAL_REASONING_AND_SKILL_EVIDENCE.md
SHA-256: 2a9104f937485060274c95adeedd269f6ebda463a77c446fd2ddd7251d89438f

# Local reasoning and skill evidence boundaries

The same loaded local model supplies sequential internal reasoning/development roles. Production uses `LocalModelReasoningAdapter` and LiteRT-LM's isolated, tool-free `streamThinking`; no cloud fallback, external account, worker network or execution capability is added.

## Cancellation and model binding

`ContinuumReasoningAdapter.cancel()` is optional for synchronous adapters and implemented by the local adapter. Development and chat cancellation reach this boundary. Adapter cancellation is sticky for one job: create a fresh adapter for a new job. Sequential passes reuse the adapter and must keep the same model ID/version and imported SHA-256 metadata. A changed model fails closed. The hash binds loaded catalog metadata; it is not a new hash verification of the multi-gigabyte file during every pass. Existing catalog byte verification at import/load remains mandatory.

Before dispatch and during completion waits, the adapter checks cancellation, thread interruption, wall-clock deadline and monotonic elapsed time. Waits poll at 10ms intervals without relying on a native Cancelled/Completed event. Each adapter pass is capped at 60 seconds independently; the callers' existing total-job/call/prompt/output bounds remain in force. Tool events invalidate a pass, including events delivered synchronously after completion. Late text/terminal callbacks cannot append returned text. Native `streamThinking` setup and `cancelProcess` themselves may block; JVM fakes cannot prove native-call latency or lifecycle safety on a device.

The Activity retains the single-assistant lane until a worker completes. Per-turn chat cancellation prevents fallback inference or tool-recovery inference after Stop. The bounded orchestrator checks cancellation at state transitions; cancelled output cannot become a successful learned experience. ToolGate continues to govern all device actions. Cancellation cannot undo a side effect already started outside the app.

## Experience evidence

`ExperienceCompiler` counts unique experience IDs. Exact repeated records count once; conflicting records sharing an ID reject the entire compilation, before eligibility filtering. Success rate, mean evaluation score and occurrence thresholds use only unique evidence. Candidate construction rejects duplicated/blank evidence IDs and an attempt to remove mandatory owner approval. Destructive sequences remain blocked.

This remains candidate preparation, not automatic skill promotion or proof that model-evaluated records are true. The compiler is not yet connected to an owner-review UI or durable promotion transaction. Future promotion must validate provenance and execution receipts through the existing owner/memory policies. No new persistent memory writes or autonomous execution are introduced.

## Verification and limitations

Regression tests use actual project classes and scripted runtime events. They test local-model boundary cancellation/deadlines/model binding, orchestrator cancellation and evidence replay/conflicts. They do not measure intelligence, compare models or prove device behavior. Use the real `gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest --stacktrace` and `gradle :app:assembleDebug --stacktrace` for release evidence, matched to the live commit and APK workflow artifact.

No third-party implementation was copied and no dependency was added. Lumo remains outside this repository change; no integration or cross-repository authority is enabled.

FILE 348/375: docs/MEMORY_AND_MODEL_ECOLOGY.md
SHA-256: 9961a3d5640e52d6aefa1526b9f2dc9bf27cd4bce8b0a59b3e85f21ed61f2519
============================================================================
# Memory and Model Ecology

This document describes the provider-neutral cognitive foundation in
`at.heinz.deviceai.cognitive`. It is deliberately not connected to `MainActivity`,
the Shizuku bridge, or a real model provider.

## Memory, provenance, and claims

`MemoryRecord` is a typed record with provenance, confidence, timestamps, tags,
parent IDs, optional source reference, validation state, and privacy class.
`InMemoryMemoryStore` rejects duplicate IDs. `MemoryRetriever` uses deterministic
token overlap and stable ID tie-breaking; callers can restrict its privacy classes.
`MemoryGraph` stores directed typed relations.

Model-generated records and claims default to `UNVERIFIED`; they cannot be
constructed as verified facts without an explicit validation path. `Claim.validated`
requires independent evidence references for verification. Claim relationships
distinguish support, contradiction, and supersession.

`MemoryWritePolicy` prevents routine interactions from becoming durable memory.
Explicit requests and reusable/durable knowledge can be retained; personal,
sensitive, and device information is assigned `PRIVATE`, `SENSITIVE`, or
`DEVICE_LOCAL_ONLY`, respectively.

## Experiences, adapters, and routing

`Experience` is an immutable evaluation record containing task/request summaries,
memory/model/source/tool references, plan and result summaries, failures, retries,
scores, feedback, confidence changes, outcome, and timestamps. The in-memory store
retrieves similar requests within the same task type using deterministic Jaccard
similarity.

`ModelAdapter` is provider-neutral. `MockModelAdapter` and `TestModelAdapter` are
local deterministic test implementations; no network adapter is included.
`ModelReputationStore` applies bounded exponential updates only to evaluated
evidence, partitioned by model, capability, and domain. `ModelRouter` selects but
does not invoke adapters. Routing plans expose strategy, model IDs, rationale,
confidence, and evidence. Self-model confidence influences whether uncertain
capabilities use multiple adapters.

## Source trust

`SourceIdentity` includes a domain, and `SourceTrustStore` maintains separate,
initially uncertain profiles per identity/domain. Accuracy, freshness,
corroboration, contradiction, and correction evidence update gradually, and
unevaluated observations are rejected. Profile confidence starts at zero and grows
gradually with evaluated claims.

## Local persistence and integrity

`CognitiveArchiveStore` accepts a caller-supplied app-private directory (Android
callers should supply `Context.filesDir`). Its versioned binary format serializes
only explicitly enumerated `IdentityState`, `CognitiveGenome`, memory, and
experience fields; it does not deserialize arbitrary classes. It validates
archive size, schema, identity/genome binding, integrity hash, forbidden genome
flags, duplicate IDs, enum values, and numeric ranges. Writes use a temporary
file and atomic replacement where supported.
The prior valid primary file is retained as last-known-good state, and loading
falls back to it when the primary is corrupt. Import/export is deterministic
Base64 over the validated archive.

`IdentityState.integrityHash` and `contentHash` are deterministic SHA-256
integrity/content hashes, not signatures. `IdentitySigner` separates authenticity
from hashing; no production signing key or Android Keystore adapter is included.
A fixed-key signer exists only in JVM tests.

## Status and limitations

- Implemented: in-memory memory/experience stores, deterministic retrieval,
  memory and claim relations, provenance/validation, privacy write policy,
  provider-neutral test adapters, evaluated reputation and source trust,
  explainable routing, and versioned archive persistence/recovery.
- Not implemented: Android Keystore signing, production model adapters,
  persistence adapters for standalone model/source trust stores, automatic
  background retention/compaction, or production UI wiring.
- Trust values and retrieval ranking are deliberately simple initial policies,
  not calibrated production recommendations.

FILE 349/375: docs/NEURAL_CONTINUITY.md
SHA-256: d158093ee54f4ab6802014148acd2bb84f654aa114e3073f6c2b4ea0087e9320

# Continuum: real shared neural learning

The scheduled runner now performs gradient updates to the same 4,113-parameter
SWB1 encoder used by Android. The initial weights come from the project's own
seeded Java-compatible random initializer. No pretrained weights or paid model
API is involved. This is a small intent/representation learner, not a generative
language model or evidence of consciousness.

## Data and promotion

Each round alternates supervised greeting/question examples with positive and
negative semantic pairs. Public research adds weak title/excerpt supervision at
one eighth of the semantic steps. Public source pairs do not become verified
facts. Private owner lessons and generated replies never enter weight training.

A 96-entry hash-priority replay reservoir retains older source experiences.
Every record carries source URL, timestamp, SHA-256, trust and replay status.
The fixed CPU budget is 12,000 attempted steps (hard cap 24,000), at most 30
seconds. Candidate checkpoints are examined every 1,000 steps. Both task
accuracies, both losses, replay retention and the existing Android validation
slice constrain promotion. Rejected candidates leave active weights byte-identical.

A separate 20-intent/20-semantic audit is evaluated for reporting only. It is not
used for gradient updates or checkpoint selection. All phrases are authored
in this repository; this is a small internal benchmark, not independent external
certification. Repeatedly reused validation can overfit over days. Future research
must add fresh, independently authored audit sets before claiming broader gains.
Activity, source counts and internal rewards are not model intelligence scores.

## Persistence and operation

`.continuum/state.json` on `continuum-state` remains the checksummed canonical
state, including active and previous model weights, experiences and 64 reports.
The workflow commits state and the public export together, serializes writers
and fails on a failed state fetch instead of replacing existing memory.

The existing four-hour schedule must live on the default branch. Its checkout
should be pinned to a CI-verified implementation commit. A PR workflow alone
cannot activate scheduled execution. `workflow_dispatch` and a change to this
workflow on the development branch also exercise one complete learning cycle.

Copilot installation and the `copilot-requests` permission have been removed;
`CONTINUUM_COPILOT=0`. GitHub-hosted runner availability and private-repository
included minutes depend on the account. Four-minute job bounds and 7-day export
retention reduce usage, but do not establish a billing hard limit. No billing
settings are changed. Schedules can be delayed by GitHub.

## Console on Issue 20

Only the repository owner's comments mutate state. Ordinary messages and
`/chat <text>` use bounded contextual retrieval with neural reranking. Follow-up
references reuse the last topic. Replies quote owner lessons or explicitly cited
source observations and identify their origin. The dialogue is template-based;
it does not pretend to be a large generative model. Unknown topics are admitted.

- `/research <question>`, `/ask <question>`, `/deep <question>`: explicit research.
- `/learn <text>`: private owner lesson (memory only).
- `/neural`, `/progress`, `/status`: model and evidence measurements.
- `/train`: one bounded neural round, respecting pause.
- `/pause`, `/resume`: pause/resume scheduled research and training.

Every third autonomous target may use the learned encoder's uncertainty to
choose an under-explored source for independent follow-up. Existing Baby Core
and World Model planning remain responsible for the other target selections.
Uncertainty is a heuristic, not calibrated epistemic confidence.

## Android

Download `neural-public.bin` from the workflow's public-model artifact (or the
state branch). Open **Continuum Learning Core v2 → GEWICHTE IMPORTIEREN** and
select that file. The importer reads at most 32,961 bytes, verifies SWB1/checksum,
reproduces both local holdouts and checks confirmed personal intent replay.
It installs only an improving nonregressing candidate. Personal memories,
command mappings and permissions remain on the device and are never uploaded.
Checksum proves integrity, not publisher authenticity; import is owner-selected.
The imported model feeds the existing local intent/uncertainty path and remains
available offline. Local training now protects the other task sharing embeddings.

## Reproduce

Run `node --test .github/continuum/*.test.mjs` and
`gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug`.
The committed SWB1 fixture has cross-runtime numeric inference, tokenization,
round-trip, corruption and personal-memory preservation tests. The example
report in `neural-benchmark-example.json` is a deterministic offline run, not
an assertion about the current live state. Re-run `neural-benchmark.mjs` to
refresh it and the JavaScript-generated Kotlin fixture.

# Adoption Backlog

## Part 3
Finish typed memory/provenance/experience/model reputation/source trust/local persistence/tests.

## Part 4
Build typed skills, bounded AgentOrchestrator, tool proposal→validation→execution→result pipeline, read-only web research provider, source-aware claim extraction, bounded retry/reflection and checkpoint/resume.

## Part 5
Build `LocalModelRuntime`, LiteRT-LM adapter first, model catalog/import, streaming local chat, structured function/tool-call parsing, cancellation and metrics. Prove with one small local model and no cloud LLM dependency.

## Part 6
Wire local model → memory → plan → tool gate → result → evaluation → memory. Add online read-only research, offline mode, local personality prompt from validated identity state, Fold-ready chat UI, APK artifact and runtime evidence.

## Later
llama.cpp backend, local embeddings, voice, multimodal, model benchmarking/router and carefully bounded multi-model experiments.

FILE 353/375: docs/open_source_reference_pack/AGENT_ORCHESTRATION.md
SHA-256: 9259491eaf1b4a356e5eee7406922bac6c5022e94b63231470e9fedc5ae8aaf0
============================================================================
# Bounded Agent Orchestration

Implement a small Kotlin state machine inspired by durable agent frameworks:

`OBSERVE → RETRIEVE → PLAN → MODEL → VALIDATE → TOOL_PROPOSAL? → GATED_EXECUTION → OBSERVE_RESULT → EVALUATE → STORE_EXPERIENCE → RESPOND`

Every step emits typed state/audit events.

## Checkpoints
- checkpoint after expensive or irreversible steps;
- persist only allowlisted schema-versioned state;
- validate on resume;
- never deserialize arbitrary executable classes;
- recover from process death using last valid checkpoint.

## Tool approval
Model-generated calls are proposals only. Execution stays behind Device AI ToolRegistry, typed schemas, permissions and Shizuku boundary. Never expose raw unrestricted shell to the model.

## Bounded reflection
Adapt Reflexion as a repair policy:
- default maximum 1–2 repair attempts;
- retry only for concrete evaluated failures;
- store structured failure/evidence/correction;
- successful lesson may become evaluated experience;
- exhaustion surfaces a blocker.

No open-ended autonomous loop.

============================================================================
FILE 354/375: docs/open_source_reference_pack/ANDROID_APP_PATTERNS.md

# Android Patterns to Adapt

Google AI Edge Gallery is the primary concrete Android reference for:
- model manager/ViewModel separation;
- per-model chat state;
- local model import/download lifecycle;
- thinking/content message separation;
- inference metrics;
- capability-gated UI;
- agent skill/tool-call presentation;
- local task modules;
- model benchmarking.

Proposed Device AI boundaries:

```
at.heinz.deviceai.localmodel
  LocalModelRuntime
  ModelDescriptor
  LiteRtLmRuntime
  LlamaCppRuntime
  ModelInstallManager
  ModelCatalog
  InferenceMetrics

at.heinz.deviceai.agent
  AgentOrchestrator
  AgentState
  AgentCheckpoint
  AgentPolicy
  ReflectionPolicy

at.heinz.deviceai.research
  ResearchProvider
  HttpReadOnlyResearchProvider
  ResearchDocument

at.heinz.deviceai.cognitive
  identity / memory / experience / source trust / router

at.heinz.deviceai.tools
  controlled tool registry / risk gate / Shizuku adapters
```

Lifecycle: inference off main thread, explicit cancellation, no Activity leaks in cognitive state, app-private persistence, low-memory recovery, and model files separated from identity/memory.

FILE 355/375: docs/open_source_reference_pack/LICENSING_AND_COPY_RULES.md
SHA-256: 42847d3a4c60d71aa537ca7a5d2eb43252c28f7bd9b1088d76c672bfe541bf2b
============================================================================
# Licensing and Copy Rules

Selected upstream projects use permissive licenses at the pinned revisions in SOURCE_INDEX.md.

Rules:
1. Prefer pattern-level adaptation and small ports.
2. Before copying source code, inspect the exact source file for extra headers/notices.
3. Preserve required copyright/license notices.
4. Record upstream repo, file path and pinned SHA for non-trivial copied code.
5. Keep exact upstream license texts under `licenses/`.
6. Model weights have separate licenses; verify every model before bundling/distribution.
7. Do not copy trademarks, branding, screenshots or product identity.
8. Avoid verbatim upstream documentation when a concise engineering summary is enough.
9. Direct reuse must remain reviewable and replaceable behind Device AI interfaces.

This is an engineering compliance checklist, not legal advice.

============================================================================
FILE 356/375: docs/open_source_reference_pack/LOCAL_INFERENCE.md
SHA-256: b11b105a185af35b9438b032b9a6052c9cef4aac3095023940c700cd1bf78fef
============================================================================
# Local Inference Adoption Plan

## Primary: LiteRT-LM
Create a provider-neutral `LocalModelRuntime` and isolated `LiteRtLmRuntime`.

Required capabilities:
- load/unload local model;
- expose metadata/capabilities;
- create/reset conversation;
- stream output with Kotlin Flow/callback abstraction;
- cancel generation;
- expose token/context/memory/latency metrics;
- accept structured tool definitions when supported;
- parse tool-call output as data without executing tools;
- choose CPU/GPU/NPU by capability/operator policy;
- fail closed and recover safely.

Use Google AI Edge Gallery for model catalog/import/download/lifecycle patterns. Model downloads are operator-controlled, checksum validated and stored separately from identity/memory.

## Secondary: llama.cpp
After the runtime interface is stable, add a GGUF backend experiment to prove backend interchangeability and benchmark CPU/Vulkan/OpenCL/other supported mobile paths.

## Alternate: ExecuTorch
Evaluate after the first working local path, especially for models/export flows that materially outperform the primary backend.

## Acceptance
Inference must require no network once model bytes exist locally. Invalid model bytes are rejected. Tool calls never bypass Device AI's ToolRegistry/risk gate.

FILE 357/375: docs/open_source_reference_pack/MEMORY_IDENTITY.md
SHA-256: b536d2e84d0a03267d61b1029697109b8d910513bce619dd61e6b01f0af44716
============================================================================
# Memory, Identity and Learning Patterns

Keep Device AI's typed memory layers: WORKING, EPISODIC, SEMANTIC, PROCEDURAL, SELF, MODEL and SOURCE.

## Letta patterns to adapt
- compact always-available identity/persona core;
- larger deferred/reference memory;
- separate skill/procedure memory;
- memory-maintenance pipeline separate from answer generation;
- conflict repair rather than silent overwrite;
- targeted edits preserve unrelated memory;
- never persist secrets or ephemeral task logs as durable memory.

Android canonical storage remains typed app-private data, not a Markdown filesystem.

## Mem0 patterns to adapt
Explainable retrieval fusion:
- lexical/BM25-like signal;
- semantic/embedding signal when a local embedding model exists;
- entity-link signal;
- temporal relevance;
- source/validation quality;
- privacy eligibility;
- usefulness/recency.

Return score components for debugging.

## Write policy
A conversation is not automatically a memory. Durable writes require an explicit reason such as accepted preference/correction, stable user fact, reusable successful procedure, evaluated experience, sourced fact, or validated self-model update.

Generated guesses remain inference/unverified until corroborated.

FILE 358/375: docs/open_source_reference_pack/README.md
SHA-256: 5dcd9aed9a2b0258474433e17713a56caa9364cfc612c9456da49400adf8d8b8
============================================================================
# Device AI — Open-Source Engineering Reference Pack

This pack is the implementation guide for reusing proven public AI/agent engineering ideas in Device AI.

Priority:
1. Google AI Edge Gallery + LiteRT-LM for Android local inference.
2. llama.cpp as fallback/benchmark backend.
3. Letta + Mem0 for memory/identity/retrieval patterns.
4. LangGraph + Microsoft Agent Framework for checkpoints, retries, tool approval and orchestration.
5. Reflexion only for bounded self-review.
6. ExecuTorch as an alternate runtime benchmark.

The first rough prototype is complete only when it runs a local model on Android, persists identity/memory locally, streams chat, proposes structured tool calls, routes device actions through the existing Shizuku risk gate, can perform read-only web research when online, and retains reduced useful behavior offline.

Do not vendor whole frameworks by default. Prefer small Android-native adapters and ports. Preserve required upstream notices for any direct code reuse.

============================================================================

FILE 372/375: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-neural-continuity.md
SHA-256: 879f2db1fbc523ddceb9423ef57bbebbca25a1fcb96c7b9e595867416ca5d0ac
============================================================================
# Neural continuity

The owner authorizes autonomous architecture and implementation on PR #19. Deliver actual bounded gradient training on GitHub, persistent replay and compatible Android weights without pretrained models, paid model APIs or uploading device data.

Reuse the Kotlin SWB1 encoder (256 buckets, 16 dimensions, shared intent and semantic heads) in JavaScript. Preserve byte-compatible snapshots and test cross-runtime inference. Alternate intent and semantic training; reject candidates if either validation task or replay retention regresses. Keep a separate audit set out of both gradients and promotion decisions. These are small authored benchmarks, not external certification or general intelligence measures.

Persist public source experiences with provenance and hashes, a bounded balanced replay buffer, last-known-good weights and per-round measurements inside existing checksummed state. Public title/excerpt pairs are weak topical supervision, never truth labels. Owner messages, private memories and generated answers cannot enter exported weights. Integrate neural reranking and contextual conversation into Baby Core retrieval, leaving explicit research commands intact.

Android imports the owner's selected bounded SWB1 file, independently evaluates both local holdouts and confirmed intent replay, and replaces only encoder weights when gates pass. It never replaces personal facts, mappings or device permissions. Local training must also guard the other task sharing the embeddings.

Keep the existing 4-hour schedule, disable paid Copilot use, serialize state writers, fail closed on damaged/missing existing state. Activate by pinning the default-branch workflow to the tested commit after CI. Actions availability and free allowance cannot be guaranteed by source code.
